title.zh: 卷二百七十二 列傳第三十一 楊業子:延昭 等 附:王貴 荊罕儒從孙:嗣 曹光實從子:克明 張暉 司超
title.en: Volume 272 Biographies 31: Yang Ye and sons: Yanzhao and others, relative: Wang Gui, Jing Hanru and nephew: Si, Cao Guangshi and nephew: Keming, Zhang Hui, Si Chao
title.raw: 卷二百七十二 列傳第三十一 楊業子:延昭 等 附:王貴 荊罕儒從孙:嗣 曹光實從子:克明 張暉 司超 Volume 272 Biographies 31: Yang Ye and sons: Yanzhao and others, relative: Wang Gui, Jing Hanru and nephew: Si, Cao Guangshi and nephew: Keming, Zhang Hui, Si Chao

sentences.zh: 楊業，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Yang Ye was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye came from Taiyuan in Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 父信，為漢麟州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xin had been prefect of Lin in Han.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin had served as prefect of Lin under the Northern Han.

sentences.zh: 業幼倜儻任俠，善騎射，好畋獵，所獲倍於人。

translations.literal: When young Ye was free-spirited and chivalrous, skilled at mounted archery, fond of hunting, and took twice as much game as others.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yang Ye was bold and adventurous, an expert horseman and archer who loved the chase and routinely bagged twice what his companions did.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂其徒曰：「我他日為將用兵，亦猶用鷹犬逐雉兔爾。」

translations.literal: He once said to his followers: "When I later become a general and employ troops in war, it will be just like using hawks and hounds to pursue pheasants and hares."
translations.idiomatic: He once told his companions, "When I command armies someday, it will be no different from hunting game with hawk and hound."

sentences.zh: 弱冠事劉崇，為保衛指揮使，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: In his early manhood he served Liu Chong as commandant of the Imperial Guard and was known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: In early adulthood he entered Liu Chong's service as a guard commander and won fame for his ferocity in battle.

sentences.zh: 累遷至建雄軍節度使，屢立戰功，所向克捷，國人號為「無敵」。

translations.literal: He rose through successive promotions to military commissioner of the Jianxiong Army, repeatedly achieved military merit, prevailed wherever he marched, and the people of the state called him "Invincible."
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become military commissioner of the Jianxiong Army, won victory after victory, and his countrymen dubbed him the Invincible General.

sentences.zh: 太宗征太原，素聞其名，嘗購求之。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Taiyuan he had long heard Yang Ye's name and had once sought to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong besieged Taiyuan, he had long coveted this renowned commander and had tried to recruit him.

sentences.zh: 既而孤壘甚危，業勸其主繼元降，以保生聚。

translations.literal: When the isolated fortress grew very perilous, Ye urged his lord Jiyuan to surrender in order to preserve the living populace.
translations.idiomatic: As the isolated city faced ruin, Yang Ye urged his sovereign Liu Jiyuan to surrender and spare the lives of the people.

sentences.zh: 繼元既降，帝遣中使召見業，大喜，以為右領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: After Jiyuan had surrendered, the emperor sent a palace envoy to summon Ye for an audience, was greatly pleased, and appointed him Grand General of the Right Vanguard Army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiyuan had submitted, the emperor summoned Yang Ye, received him with delight, and made him a senior general of the Right Vanguard Guard.

sentences.zh: 師還，授鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was made prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was appointed prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 帝以業老于邊事，復遷代州兼三交駐泊兵馬都部署，帝密封橐裝，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: Because the emperor regarded Ye as experienced in frontier affairs, he was again transferred to Daizhou and concurrently made overall commander of the garrison forces stationed at Sanjiao, and the emperor sealed a pouch of gifts for him with a very generous grant.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yang Ye's long experience on the frontier, the emperor reassigned him to Daizhou as overall commander of the Sanjiao garrison and sent him a sealed pouch of rewards of exceptional value.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入雁門，業領麾下數千騎自西陘而出，由小陘至雁門北口，南向背擊之，契丹大敗。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Yanmen Pass, Ye led several thousand horsemen under his command out through the western defile, went by the small defile to the northern mouth of Yanmen, and struck them from the south from behind; the Khitan suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan broke through Yanmen Pass, Yang Ye led several thousand cavalry out the western route, swung through the lesser pass to the north gate, and hit them from the south in a rear attack, routing them completely.

sentences.zh: 以功遷雲州觀察使，仍判鄭州、代州。

translations.literal: For this merit he was promoted to observation commissioner of Yunzhou and still concurrently administered Zhengzhou and Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he was promoted to observation commissioner of Yun while retaining concurrent charge of Zheng and Dai.

sentences.zh: 自是，契丹望見業旌旗即引去。

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever the Khitan saw Ye's banners and flags they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the Khitan withdrew at the mere sight of Yang Ye's banners.

sentences.zh: 主將戍邊者多忌之，有潛上謗書斥言其短，帝覽之皆不問，封其奏以付業。

translations.literal: Many frontier commanders were jealous of him; some secretly submitted memorials slandering him and enumerating his faults, but when the emperor read them he made no inquiry and sealed each memorial and gave it to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Many frontier commanders envied him, and some secretly denounced him to the throne; the emperor read their memorials but pursued no inquiry, instead sealing each one and forwarding it to Yang Ye himself.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，大兵北征，以忠武軍節度使潘美為雲、應路行營都部署，命業副之，以西上閤門使、蔚州刺史王侁，軍器庫使、順州團練使劉文裕護其軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi a great army marched north; Pan Mei, military commissioner of the Loyal and Martial Army, was made overall commander of the Yun and Ying route field headquarters, with Ye ordered as his deputy, and Wang Yan of the Western Upper Pavilion Gate office and prefect of Yu prefecture and Liu Wenyu, commissioner of the armory depot and regimental trainer of Shun prefecture, were assigned to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi the court launched a major northern campaign, naming Pan Mei supreme commander of the Yun–Ying route with Yang Ye as his deputy, while Wang Yan and Liu Wenyu were assigned as army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 諸軍連拔雲、應、寰、朔四州，師次桑乾河，會曹彬之師不利，諸路班師，美等歸代州。

translations.literal: The armies in succession captured the four prefectures of Yun, Ying, Huan, and Shuo; the force halted at the Sanggan River; when Cao Bin's army met with misfortune all routes withdrew, and Mei and the others returned to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The armies took Yun, Ying, Huan, and Shuo in succession and halted on the Sanggan, but when Cao Bin's column faltered every route was ordered home and Pan Mei withdrew to Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔遷四州之民於內地，令美等以所部之兵護之。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered the relocation of the populace of the four prefectures to the interior, and directed Mei and the others to escort them with the troops under their command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the court ordered the four prefectures' populations moved inland and directed Pan Mei and his colleagues to escort them with their troops.

sentences.zh: 時契丹國母蕭氏與其大臣耶律漢甯、南北皮室及五押惕隱領眾十餘萬，復陷寰州。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan empress dowager Lady Xiao, together with her ministers Yelü Hanning, the northern and southern pishi, and the five yatixin, led a force of more than one hundred thousand and again took Huan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan empress dowager Xiao, her minister Yelü Hanning, the northern and southern palace guards, and the five yatixin chiefs then led more than a hundred thousand men and recaptured Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 業謂美等曰：「今遼兵益盛，不可與戰。

translations.literal: Ye said to Mei and the others: "The Liao forces are now stronger than ever; we must not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye told Pan Mei and the others, "The Liao army is stronger than ever—we must not fight them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷止令取數州之民，但領兵出大石路，先遣人密告雲、朔州守將，俟大軍離代州日，令雲州之眾先出。

translations.literal: The court has only ordered us to bring out the people of several prefectures; we need only lead the army out by the Dashi route, first send men in secret to inform the defending generals of Yun and Shuo, and when the main army leaves Daizhou on that day have Yunzhou's populace come out first.
translations.idiomatic: The court only wants the civilians of these prefectures brought out. Lead the army along the Dashi road and secretly warn the garrison commanders of Yun and Shuo; the day we march from Daizhou, Yunzhou's people should move out first.

sentences.zh: 我師次應州，契丹必來拒，即令朔州民出城，直入石碣谷。

translations.literal: When our army halts at Yingzhou the Khitan are sure to come to oppose us; then have the people of Shuozhou leave the city and go straight into Shijie Valley.
translations.idiomatic: When we reach Yingzhou the Khitan will certainly block us; then Shuozhou's people should leave the city and march straight into Shijie Valley.

sentences.zh: 遣強弩千人列于谷口，以騎士援于中路，則三州之眾，保萬全矣。」

translations.literal: Send a thousand strong crossbowmen to line the mouth of the valley and post cavalry in support along the middle route, and then the masses of the three prefectures will be kept entirely secure."
translations.idiomatic: Post a thousand crossbowmen at the valley mouth with cavalry in support along the middle road, and all three prefectures' people will reach safety."

sentences.zh: 侁沮其議曰：「領數萬精兵而畏懦如此。

translations.literal: Wang Yan obstructed this plan and said: "Leading tens of thousands of elite troops yet being so timid and cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan objected: "You command tens of thousands of crack troops, yet you shrink from the enemy like this.

sentences.zh: 但趨雁門北川中，鼓行而往。」

translations.literal: We need only hurry through the northern valley of Yanmen beating drums as we march."
translations.idiomatic: We should simply march with drums beating through the northern valley of Yanmen Pass."

sentences.zh: 文裕亦贊成之。

translations.literal: Wenyu also endorsed this view.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenyu agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 業曰：「不可，此必敗之勢也。」

translations.literal: Ye said: "That will not do; this is a course certain to end in defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye replied, "No—that is a plan for certain defeat."

sentences.zh: 侁曰：「君侯素號無敵，今見敵逗撓不戰，得非有他志乎？」

translations.literal: Wang Yan said: "My lord has always been called Invincible; now on seeing the enemy you hesitate and refuse battle—could it be that you have some other design?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan said, "You are called Invincible, yet now you hang back and refuse to fight—do you perhaps have other intentions?"

sentences.zh: 業曰：「業非避死，蓋時有未利，徒令殺傷士卒而功不立。

translations.literal: Ye said: "Ye is not avoiding death; it is only that the moment is not favorable, and we would merely kill and wound soldiers without establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye said, "I am not trying to escape death; the moment is simply unfavorable, and we would only slaughter our men without winning anything.

sentences.zh: 今君責業以不死，當為諸公先。」

translations.literal: Now that you gentlemen charge Ye with failure to face death, I ought to go before you all."
translations.idiomatic: Since you demand that I not shrink from death, I shall lead the way."

sentences.zh: 將行，泣謂美曰：「此行必不利。

translations.literal: As he was about to march he wept and said to Mei: "This expedition is sure to go badly.
translations.idiomatic: About to set out, he wept and told Pan Mei, "This campaign is doomed to go wrong.

sentences.zh: 業，太原降將，分當死。

translations.literal: Ye, a surrendered general of Taiyuan, ought by rights to die.
translations.idiomatic: I am a surrendered general from Taiyuan and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 上不殺，寵以連帥，授之兵柄。

translations.literal: The emperor did not kill me but favored me with a military commission and entrusted me with command of troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spared me, honored me with a military commission, and gave me command of an army.

sentences.zh: 非縱敵不擊，蓋伺其便，將立尺寸功以報國恩。

translations.literal: It was not that I let the enemy go without striking; I was waiting for the opportune moment, intending to win even a small measure of merit to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: I was not holding back from the enemy; I was waiting for the right moment to win even a small victory and repay the state's kindness.

sentences.zh: 今諸君責業以避敵，業當先死於敵。」

translations.literal: Now that you gentlemen charge Ye with shunning the enemy, Ye ought to die first among the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you accuse me of shunning the enemy, I shall die fighting in the van."

sentences.zh: 因指陳家谷口曰：「諸君于此張步兵強弩，為左右翼以援，俟業轉戰至此，即以步兵夾擊救之，不然，無遺類矣。」

translations.literal: He then pointed to the mouth of Chenjia Valley and said: "Gentlemen, here deploy infantry and strong crossbows as left and right wings to support; when Ye fights his way here in retreat, then use the infantry to strike from both sides and rescue me—otherwise there will be none left alive."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to Chenjia Valley and said, "Post infantry and crossbowmen here as left and right wings. When I fight my way back here, strike from both sides to save us—or none of us will survive."

sentences.zh: 美即與侁領麾下兵陣于谷口。

translations.literal: Mei at once led the troops under his command with Yan and arrayed them at the mouth of the valley.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei and Wang Yan then drew up their troops at the valley mouth.

sentences.zh: 自寅至巳，侁使人登托邏臺望之，以為契丹敗走，欲爭其功，即領兵離谷口。

translations.literal: From the hour yin to the hour si, Yan sent men up the watchtower to look out and thought the Khitan had been defeated and were fleeing; wishing to claim the merit, he at once led his troops away from the valley mouth.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until mid-morning Wang Yan sent men up the watchtower, mistook a Khitan retreat for a rout, and left the valley mouth to seize the glory.

sentences.zh: 美不能制，乃緣交河西南行二十里。

translations.literal: Mei could not restrain him and therefore followed the Jiao River southwest for twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei could not stop him and marched twenty li southwest along the Jiao River.

sentences.zh: 俄聞業敗，即麾兵卻走。

translations.literal: Soon hearing that Ye had been defeated, he at once waved his troops to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Yang Ye had been defeated, he immediately ordered a retreat.

sentences.zh: 業力戰，自午至暮，果至谷口。

translations.literal: Ye fought with all his strength from noon until evening and indeed reached the mouth of the valley.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye fought from noon until evening and at last reached the valley mouth.

sentences.zh: 望見無人，即拊膺大慟，再率帳下士力戰，身被數十創，士卒殆盡，業猶手刃數十百人。

translations.literal: Seeing no one there he beat his breast and wailed greatly, again led the soldiers under his command to fight with all their strength, received several tens of wounds on his body, his troops were nearly all gone, yet Ye still killed several tens or hundreds of men with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Finding no one there he beat his breast and wept, then led his personal guard back into the fight. Though he took dozens of wounds and his men were nearly all gone, he still cut down scores of the enemy with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 馬重傷不能進，遂為契丹所擒，其子延玉亦沒焉。

translations.literal: His horse was gravely wounded and could not advance, and he was thereupon captured by the Khitan; his son Yanyu also perished.
translations.idiomatic: His horse was too badly wounded to go on, and he was taken by the Khitan; his son Yanyu also fell.

sentences.zh: 業因太息曰：「上遇我厚，期討賊捍邊以報，而反為奸臣所迫，致王師敗績，何面目求活耶！」

translations.literal: Ye therefore sighed deeply and said: "The emperor treated me generously; I expected to attack bandits and defend the frontier in repayment, yet instead I was forced by treacherous ministers and caused the imperial army to suffer defeat—what face have I to seek to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye sighed and said, "The emperor treated me generously. I meant to repay him by fighting the enemy on the frontier, yet treacherous ministers forced me into this defeat. How can I face him and live?"

sentences.zh: 乃不食，三日死。

translations.literal: He then refused food and died after three days.
translations.idiomatic: He refused food and died three days later.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，痛惜甚，俄下詔曰：「執干戈而衛社稷，聞鼓鼙而思將帥。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he grieved deeply; soon he issued an edict saying: "Those who grasp weapons and guard the altars of soil and grain—when drums and war-gongs sound, one thinks of generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and soon issued an edict: "Men who take up arms to defend the realm—when war drums sound, the court thinks of its generals.

sentences.zh: 盡力死敵，立節邁倫，不有追崇，曷彰義烈！

translations.literal: To exhaust one's strength and die facing the enemy, to establish integrity surpassing ordinary men—if there is no posthumous honor, how may righteous valor be displayed!
translations.idiomatic: To spend one's last strength against the enemy and set an example beyond the common run—without posthumous honors, how can such loyalty be shown to the world!

sentences.zh: 故雲州觀察使楊業誠堅金石，氣激風雲。

translations.literal: The late observation commissioner of Yunzhou Yang Ye was in loyalty firm as metal and stone, in spirit stirring wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The late Yang Ye, observation commissioner of Yun, was loyal as metal and stone and bold as wind and storm.

sentences.zh: 挺隴上之雄才，本山西之茂族。

translations.literal: He displayed heroic talent on the Long Plateau and sprang from a flourishing clan of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A hero of the Long Plateau and scion of a great Shanxi family,

sentences.zh: 自委戎乘，式資戰功。

translations.literal: from the time he entrusted himself to chariots of war he continually contributed to military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: from the day he took up arms he won merit in battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 方提貔虎之師，以效邊陲之用。

translations.literal: He had just been leading troops fierce as tiger and bear to serve the needs of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He had just led tiger-and-bear troops to serve on the frontier

sentences.zh: 而群帥敗約，援兵不前。

translations.literal: when the commanders in mass broke their agreement and the relief troops did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: when his fellow commanders broke faith and relief never came.

sentences.zh: 獨以孤軍，陷於沙漠；

translations.literal: Alone with an isolated army he was trapped in the desert;
translations.idiomatic: Alone with a stranded army in the desert wastes,

sentences.zh: 勁果猋厲，有死不回。

translations.literal: fierce and swift as the whirlwind, he had death but would not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: he fought on like a storm and would not turn back though death was certain.

sentences.zh: 求之古人，何以加此！

translations.literal: Search among the men of old—how could one add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Among the heroes of antiquity, who could surpass this!

sentences.zh: 是用特舉徽典，以旌遺忠。

translations.literal: Therefore we specially raise these honored rites to mark his surviving loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore confer these special honors to commemorate his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，知我深意。

translations.literal: If his spirit has awareness, let it know the depth of our meaning.
translations.idiomatic: If his spirit endures, let it know how deeply we mourn him.

sentences.zh: 可贈太尉、大同軍節度，賜其家布帛千匹、粟千石。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Grand Marshal and military commissioner of the Datong Army, and his family granted one thousand bolts of cloth and silk and one thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal and military commissioner of Datong, with one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand shi of grain for his family.

sentences.zh: 大將軍潘美降三官，監軍王侁除名、隸金州，劉文裕除名、隸登州。」

translations.literal: Grand General Pan Mei is reduced three ranks; army supervisor Wang Yan is struck from the rolls and assigned to Jin prefecture; Liu Wenyu is struck from the rolls and assigned to Deng prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei is demoted three ranks; Wang Yan is struck from the rolls and banished to Jin; Liu Wenyu is struck from the rolls and banished to Deng."

sentences.zh: 業不知書，忠烈武勇，有智謀。

translations.literal: Ye did not know books, but was loyal, fierce, martial, and brave, and possessed wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye was unlettered, yet loyal, fierce, and resourceful in war.

sentences.zh: 練習攻戰，與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: He drilled in attack and battle and shared hardship and comfort with his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He trained constantly for battle and shared every hardship with his men.

sentences.zh: 代北苦寒，人多服氈罽，業但挾纊露坐治軍事，傍不設火，侍者殆僵仆，而業怡然無寒色。

translations.literal: North of Dai was bitterly cold; most men wore felt and rugs, but Ye only tucked a cotton quilt under his arm and sat in the open conducting military affairs, with no fire set beside him; attendants nearly stiffened and collapsed, yet Ye was at ease and showed no sign of cold.
translations.idiomatic: The country north of Dai was bitter cold; most men wore heavy felt, but Yang Ye would sit in the open conducting affairs with only a light quilt, no fire at his side. His attendants nearly froze stiff, yet he showed no sign of cold.

sentences.zh: 為政簡易，御下有恩，故士卒樂為之用。

translations.literal: In governing he was simple and easy, and in commanding subordinates he showed kindness, so soldiers were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was plain and fair, his treatment of men generous, and his soldiers served him gladly.

sentences.zh: 朔州之敗，麾下尚百餘人，業謂曰：「汝等各有父母妻子，與我俱死，無益也，可走還，報天子。」

translations.literal: At the defeat at Shuozhou he still had more than a hundred men under his command; Ye said to them: "You each have fathers and mothers, wives and children; to die together with me is of no benefit—you may go back and report to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At the rout at Shuozhou he still had more than a hundred men with him. He told them, "You all have parents and families. Dying with me serves no purpose—go back and report to the emperor."

sentences.zh: 眾皆感泣不肯去。

translations.literal: All were moved to tears and refused to leave.
translations.idiomatic: They wept and refused to leave him.

sentences.zh: 淄州刺史王貴殺數十人，矢盡遂死，餘亦死，無一生還者。

translations.literal: Zibo prefect Wang Gui killed several tens of men, and when his arrows were exhausted he died; the rest also died, and not one returned alive.
translations.idiomatic: Zibo prefect Wang Gui cut down dozens of the enemy before his arrows ran out and he fell; the rest died as well, and not one man returned alive.

sentences.zh: 聞者皆流涕。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard the tale wept.

sentences.zh: 業既沒，朝廷錄其子供奉官延朗為崇儀副使，次子殿直延浦、延訓竝為供奉官，延環、延貴、延彬竝為殿直。

translations.literal: After Ye had perished the court enrolled his son the palace attendant Yanlang as Vice Commissioner of Honored Rites, his second sons the palace guards Yanpu and Yanxun both as palace attendants, and Yanhuan, Yangui, and Yanbin all as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Ye's death the court promoted his son Yanlang from palace attendant to Vice Commissioner of Honored Rites, appointed his second sons Yanpu and Yanxun as palace attendants, and made Yanhuan, Yangui, and Yanbin palace guards as well.

sentences.zh: 子 延昭

translations.literal: Son: Yanzhao
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yang Yanzhao

sentences.zh: 延昭，本名延朗，後改焉。

translations.literal: Yanzhao's original name was Yanlang; it was later changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao had originally been named Yanlang and later changed his name.

sentences.zh: 幼沉默寡言，為兒時，多戲為軍陣，業嘗曰：「此兒類我。」

translations.literal: When young he was silent and spoke little; as a child he often played at forming battle arrays, and Ye once said: "This boy is like me."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quiet and reserved and loved to play at war games. Yang Ye once said, "This child takes after me."

sentences.zh: 每征行，必以從。

translations.literal: On every campaign he was sure to have him follow.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign Yang Ye took him along.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，補供奉官。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he was appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he was appointed a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 業攻應、朔，延昭為其軍先鋒，戰朔州城下，流矢貫臂，鬥益急。

translations.literal: When Ye attacked Ying and Shuo, Yanzhao served as vanguard of his army; fighting below the walls of Shuozhou a stray arrow pierced his arm, yet he fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ye attacked Ying and Shuo, Yanzhao led his vanguard. Below the walls of Shuozhou a stray arrow pierced his arm, yet he fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 以崇儀副使出知景州。

translations.literal: As Vice Commissioner of Honored Rites he was sent out to know Jing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Commissioner of Honored Rites and sent out as prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 時江、淮凶歉，命為江、淮南都巡檢使。

translations.literal: At that time the Yangzi and Huai regions suffered famine; he was appointed overall inspector of the Jiang and Huainan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Yangzi and Huai regions he was appointed overall inspector of Jiang and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 改崇儀使、知定遠軍，徙保州緣邊都巡檢使，就加如京使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner of Honored Rites and made to know Dingyuan Army, transferred to overall frontier inspector of Baozhou, and concurrently promoted to Envoy to the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of Honored Rites and made commander of Dingyuan, then transferred to overall frontier inspector of Bao and concurrently promoted to Envoy to the Capital.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年冬，契丹擾邊，延昭時在遂城。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xianping the Khitan harassed the frontier; Yanzhao was then at Suicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Xianping the Khitan raided the frontier while Yanzhao was at Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 城小無備，契丹攻之甚急，長圍數日。

translations.literal: The city was small and without preparations; the Khitan attacked it very fiercely and maintained a long siege for several days.
translations.idiomatic: The town was small and poorly defended; the Khitan pressed the attack fiercely and kept it under siege for days.

sentences.zh: 契丹每督戰，眾心危懼，延昭悉集城中丁壯登陴，賦器甲護守。

translations.literal: Whenever the Khitan pressed the assault the people's hearts were fearful; Yanzhao gathered all the able-bodied men in the city onto the battlements, issued weapons and armor, and organized the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Each Khitan assault spread panic through the town, but Yanzhao mustered every able-bodied man onto the walls, armed them, and organized the defense.

sentences.zh: 會大寒，汲水灌城上，旦悉為冰，堅滑不可上，契丹遂潰去，獲其鎧仗甚眾。

translations.literal: It happened to be bitterly cold; they drew water and poured it on the top of the wall, and by dawn all had become ice, hard and slippery so that none could climb up; the Khitan thereupon broke and fled, and they captured a great quantity of their armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: A bitter cold set in; they poured water over the walls, and by dawn the ramparts were sheeted in ice too slick to climb. The Khitan broke and fled, leaving a great store of arms behind.

sentences.zh: 以功拜莫州刺史。

translations.literal: For this merit he was appointed prefect of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he was appointed prefect of Mo.

sentences.zh: 時真宗駐大名，傅潛握重兵頓中山。

translations.literal: At that time Zhenzong was stationed at Daming; Fu Qian held a great army halted at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was then at Daming while Fu Qian held a large army idle at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 延昭與楊嗣、石普屢請益兵以戰，潛不許。

translations.literal: Yanzhao together with Yang Si and Shi Pu repeatedly requested additional troops to give battle, but Qian would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao, Yang Si, and Shi Pu repeatedly asked for reinforcements to fight, but Fu Qian refused.

sentences.zh: 及潛抵罪，召延昭赴行在，屢得對，訪以邊要。

translations.literal: When Qian was brought to account for his crime, Yanzhao was summoned to the imperial camp, repeatedly granted audiences, and consulted on frontier essentials.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Qian was punished, Yanzhao was summoned to the imperial camp, granted repeated audiences, and consulted on frontier strategy.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，指示諸王曰：「延昭父業為前朝名將，延昭治兵護塞有父風，深可嘉也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and pointed him out to the princes, saying: "Yanzhao's father Ye was a famous general of the previous reign; Yanzhao in training troops and guarding the passes has his father's manner—deeply worthy of praise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and told the princes, "Yanzhao's father Yang Ye was a famous general of the previous reign. In training troops and guarding the passes he shows his father's spirit—deeply admirable."

sentences.zh: 厚賜，遣還。

translations.literal: He was richly rewarded and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him generously and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 是冬，契丹南侵，延昭伏銳兵於羊山西，自北掩擊，且戰且退。

translations.literal: That winter the Khitan invaded south; Yanzhao hid elite troops west of Mount Yang, struck from the north in a flanking attack, and fought while retreating.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as the Khitan invaded southward, Yanzhao hid elite troops west of Mount Yang, struck from the north in a flanking attack, and fought while feigning retreat.

sentences.zh: 及山西，伏發，契丹眾大敗，獲其將，函首以獻。

translations.literal: When they reached the west of the mountain the ambush was sprung; the Khitan masses suffered a great defeat, and they captured one of their generals and presented his head in a box.
translations.idiomatic: At the western slope the ambush sprang; the Khitan army was routed, a general was captured, and his head was sent to court in a box.

sentences.zh: 進本州團練使，與保州楊嗣並命。

translations.literal: He was advanced to regimental trainer of his home prefecture, appointed together with Yang Si of Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regimental trainer of his home prefecture, Yang Si of Bao receiving the same appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰相曰：「嗣及延昭，並出疏外，以忠勇自效。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief ministers: "Si and Yanzhao both come from remote frontier regions and devote themselves through loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers, "Si and Yanzhao both come from the remote frontier and serve with loyal courage.

sentences.zh: 朝中忌嫉者眾，朕力為保庇，以及於此。」

translations.literal: In court many are jealous of them; I have exerted myself to protect them and brought them to this point."
translations.idiomatic: Many at court envy them, yet I have shielded them and brought them to their present rank."

sentences.zh: 五年，契丹侵保州，延昭與嗣提兵援之，未成列，為契丹所襲，軍士多喪失。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Khitan invaded Baozhou; Yanzhao and Si led troops to relieve it, but before they had formed their ranks they were struck by the Khitan and many soldiers were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Khitan attacked Bao; Yanzhao and Si marched to relieve it but were caught before they could form ranks and lost many men.

sentences.zh: 命李繼宣、王汀代還，將治其罪。

translations.literal: Li Jixuan and Wang Ting were ordered to replace them and return, and proceedings to punish their crimes were to be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixuan and Wang Ting were sent to replace them and bring them back for punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「嗣輩素以勇聞，將收其後效。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Si and his like have long been known for courage; we shall await their later achievements."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Si and his fellows are famed for courage; let us await what they achieve next."

sentences.zh: 即宥之。

translations.literal: He at once pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them at once.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，契丹復侵望都，繼宣逗遛不進，坐削秩，復用延昭為都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year the Khitan again invaded Wangdu; Jixuan dallied and did not advance, was punished by reduction in rank, and Yanzhao was again employed as overall inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year the Khitan again attacked Wangdu. Jixuan hung back and was demoted; Yanzhao was again made overall inspector.

sentences.zh: 時講防秋之策，詔嗣及延昭條上利害，又徙甯邊軍部署。

translations.literal: At that time they were discussing autumn-defense strategy; an edict directed Si and Yanzhao to set forth the advantages and disadvantages in detail, and Yanzhao was again transferred to frontier army deployment at Ningbian.
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated autumn-defense strategy, Si and Yanzhao were ordered to submit detailed recommendations, and Yanzhao was transferred to command the Ningbian deployment.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，詔益延昭兵滿萬人，如契丹騎入寇，則屯靜安軍之東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde an edict increased Yanzhao's troops to a full ten thousand men; if Khitan cavalry invaded, he was to encamp east of Jing'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde his force was increased to ten thousand men, with orders to encamp east of Jing'an if Khitan cavalry invaded.

sentences.zh: 令莫州部署石普屯馬村西以護屯田。

translations.literal: Mozhou deployment commander Shi Pu was ordered to encamp west of Macun to protect the frontier farms.
translations.idiomatic: Mo deployment commander Shi Pu was ordered to hold west of Macun to protect the frontier farms.

sentences.zh: 斷黑盧口、萬年橋敵騎奔沖之路，仍會諸路兵掎角追襲，令魏能、張凝、田敏奇兵牽制之。

translations.literal: They were to cut off the enemy cavalry routes of charge at Heilukou and Wannian Bridge, still join the armies of various routes in pincer pursuit, and order Wei Neng, Zhang Ning, and Tian Min with odd troops to pin the enemy down.
translations.idiomatic: They were to block the enemy cavalry at Heilukou and Wannian Bridge, coordinate pincer attacks with other columns, and assign Wei Neng, Zhang Ning, and Tian Min to tie down the enemy with diversionary forces.

sentences.zh: 時王超為都部署，聽不隸屬。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Chao was overall deployment commander and was not subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao was then supreme deployment commander and did not answer to him.

sentences.zh: 延昭上言：「契丹頓澶淵，去北境千里，人馬俱乏，雖眾易敗，凡有剽掠，率在馬上。

translations.literal: Yanzhao submitted a memorial: "The Khitan are halted at Chanyuan, a thousand li from the northern frontier; men and horses are both exhausted—though numerous they are easy to defeat. Whatever plunder they take is generally done on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao memorialized: "The Khitan are camped at Chanyuan, a thousand li from our border, their men and horses exhausted. Though numerous, they can be beaten, for they do all their raiding from horseback.

sentences.zh: 願飭諸軍，扼其要路，眾可殲焉，即幽、易數州，可襲而取。」

translations.literal: I wish to order the armies to seize their vital routes so the masses may be destroyed; then the several prefectures of You and Yi may be taken by surprise attack."
translations.idiomatic: Order our forces to hold their vital routes and we can destroy them, then strike and seize You and Yi."

sentences.zh: 奏入，不報，乃率兵抵遼境，破古城，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered there was no response; he thereupon led troops to the Liao border, broke Gucheng, and captured heads and prisoners in great number.
translations.idiomatic: The court never replied, so he marched into Liao territory, stormed Gucheng, and took many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 及請和，真宗選邊州守臣，御筆錄以示宰相，命延昭知保州兼緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When peace was requested, Zhenzong selected frontier prefects, recorded them with the imperial brush to show the chief ministers, and appointed Yanzhao to know Baozhou and concurrently overall frontier inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was made, Zhenzong personally selected frontier commanders for the chief ministers and appointed Yanzhao prefect of Bao and overall frontier inspector.

sentences.zh: 二年，追敘守禦之勞，進本州防禦使，俄徙高陽關副都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year, in recognition of his merit in defense, he was advanced to defense commissioner of his home prefecture and soon transferred to deputy overall deployment of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, for his defensive service, he was promoted to defense commissioner of his home prefecture, then transferred to deputy commander of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 在屯所九年，延昭不達吏事，軍中牒訴，常遣小校周正治之，頗為正所罔，因緣為奸。

translations.literal: For nine years at his garrison post Yanzhao was unskilled in administrative affairs; military petitions and lawsuits in the army he often sent the junior officer Zhou Zheng to handle, and Zheng greatly deceived him, taking advantage to commit wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: For nine years at his post Yanzhao was no administrator; he left army lawsuits to a junior officer named Zhou Zheng, who deceived him and used the post for private gain.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，斥正還營而戒延昭焉。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it, rebuked Zheng and sent him back to camp while admonishing Yanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he dismissed Zheng and warned Yanzhao.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 延昭智勇善戰，所得奉賜悉犒軍，未嘗問家事。

translations.literal: Yanzhao was wise, brave, and skilled in battle; all stipends and rewards he received he used entirely to reward the army and never inquired into household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was wise and brave in battle; he spent every stipend and reward on his troops and never troubled himself with household affairs.

sentences.zh: 出入騎從如小校，號令嚴明，與士卒同甘苦，遇敵必身先，行陣克捷，推功于下，故人樂為用。

translations.literal: Going out and in he rode with attendants like a junior officer; his commands were strict and clear, he shared hardship and comfort with soldiers, whenever he met the enemy he always went first, in battle arrays he achieved victory, and pushed merit down to subordinates, so men were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with only a small escort like any junior officer, commanded with iron discipline, shared every hardship with his men, always led the charge, won his battles, and credited his subordinates—so his soldiers followed him gladly.

sentences.zh: 在邊防二十餘年，契丹憚之，目為楊六郎。

translations.literal: On the frontier defense for more than twenty years the Khitan feared him and called him the Sixth Son Yang.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years on the frontier the Khitan feared him and called him Yang the Sixth Son.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝嗟悼之，遣中使護櫬以歸，河朔之人多望柩而泣。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor sighed and mourned him, sent a palace envoy to escort the coffin home, and many people north of the Yellow River looked toward the bier and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor mourned him deeply, sent a palace envoy to escort his coffin home, and people across the Hebei plain wept as it passed.

sentences.zh: 錄其三子官，其常從、門客亦試藝甄敘之。

translations.literal: Three of his sons were enrolled in office, and his regular followers and retainers were also tested in the arts and given appointments according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons were given offices, and his staff and retainers were examined and appointed according to merit.

sentences.zh: 子文廣。

translations.literal: Son: Wenguang.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yang Wenguang.

sentences.zh: 孫 文廣

translations.literal: Grandson: Wenguang
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Yang Wenguang

sentences.zh: 文廣，字仲容。

translations.literal: Wenguang, style name Zhongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenguang, whose style name was Zhongrong,

sentences.zh: 以班行討賊張海有功，授殿直。

translations.literal: As a guardsman in rank he campaigned against the bandit Zhang Hai with merit and was appointed palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: served as a guardsman against the bandit Zhang Hai, won merit, and was made a palace guard.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹宣撫陝西，與語奇之，置麾下。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan as pacification commissioner of Shaanxi spoke with him, found him remarkable, and placed him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, was struck by him in conversation and took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 從狄青南征，知德順軍，為廣西鈐轄，知宜、邕二州，累遷左藏庫使、帶御器械。

translations.literal: He followed Di Qing on the southern campaign, was made to know Deshun Army, became Guangxi military commissioner, knew Yi and Yong prefectures, and was repeatedly promoted to Left Treasury commissioner and Bearer of Imperial Arms.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Di Qing south, commanded Deshun, became Guangxi military commissioner and prefect of Yi and Yong, and rose to Left Treasury commissioner and Bearer of Imperial Arms.

sentences.zh: 治平中，議宿衛將，英宗曰：「文廣，名將後，且有功。」

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era, when discussing palace guard generals, Yingzong said: "Wenguang is the descendant of a famous general and moreover has merit."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era, when the court discussed palace guard generals, Yingzong said, "Wenguang is the son of a famous house and has earned his place."

sentences.zh: 乃擢成州團練使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使，遷興州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to regimental trainer of Chengzhou and overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard, and transferred to defense commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regimental trainer of Cheng and overall commander of the Dragon Divine Guard, then made defense commissioner of Xing.

sentences.zh: 秦鳳副都總管韓琦使築篳篥城，文廣聲言城噴珠，率眾急趣篳篥，比暮至其所，部分已定。

translations.literal: Han Qi as deputy overall commander of Qinfeng ordered the building of Bilei city; Wenguang declared the city was Penzhu, led the masses in haste to Bilei, and by evening reached the place—the dispositions were already set.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, deputy commander of Qinfeng, ordered Bilei built; Wenguang spread word that the site was Penzhu, rushed his troops there, and by evening had the defenses in place.

sentences.zh: 遲明，敵騎大至，知不可犯而去，遺書曰：「當白國主，以數萬精騎逐汝。」

translations.literal: At dawn enemy cavalry came in great force, saw they could not attack and left, leaving a letter saying: "I shall report to the state lord and have tens of thousands of elite cavalry pursue you."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a large enemy force arrived, saw the position was impregnable, and withdrew, leaving a note: "I shall tell our lord to send tens of thousands of elite horsemen after you."

sentences.zh: 文廣遣將襲之，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Wenguang sent generals to strike them and beheaded and captured a great number.
translations.idiomatic: Wenguang sent troops in pursuit and took many heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，文廣曰：「先人有奪人之氣。

translations.literal: When asked the reason, Wenguang said: "My forebears had the spirit to seize others' morale.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Wenguang said, "My forebears taught me to seize the enemy's spirit first.

sentences.zh: 此必爭之地，彼若知而據之，則未可圖也。」

translations.literal: This is ground that must be contested; if they knew and held it, it could not then be taken."
translations.idiomatic: This was contested ground; had they seized it first, we could never have taken it."

sentences.zh: 詔書褒諭，賜襲衣、帶、馬。

translations.literal: An edict praised and rewarded him, granting court robes, belt, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him in an edict and granted robes, a belt, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 知涇州、鎮戎軍，為定州路副都總管，遷步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was made to know Jingzhou and Zhenrong Army, became deputy overall commander of the Dingzhou route, and was transferred to chief adjutant of the Foot Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Jing and commander of Zhenrong, then deputy overall commander of the Ding route and chief adjutant of the Foot Army.

sentences.zh: 遼人爭代州地界，文廣獻陣圖並取幽燕策，未報而卒，贈同州觀察使。

translations.literal: The Liao disputed the border of Daizhou; Wenguang submitted battle arrays and a plan to take You and Yan, but before a response arrived he died and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao disputed Daizhou's border he submitted battle plans and a strategy for You and Yan, but died before the court replied and was posthumously made observation commissioner of Tong.

sentences.zh: 附 王貴

translations.literal: Appended: Wang Gui
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wang Gui

sentences.zh: 王貴者，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Gui was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui came from Taiyuan in Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補衛士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was appointed a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangshun era he joined the guard.

sentences.zh: 宋初，累遷至散員都指揮使、馬步軍都軍頭，領勝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Song he was repeatedly promoted to overall commander of the scattered guards and overall commander of the horse and foot armies, and held Shengzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he rose to command the scattered guards and the horse-and-foot armies and served as prefect of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，出為淄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he went out as prefect of Zibo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was sent out as prefect of Zibo.

sentences.zh: 受詔從潘美北征，攻沁州，頗立戰功。

translations.literal: Receiving orders he followed Pan Mei on the northern campaign, attacked Qin prefecture, and achieved considerable military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered north with Pan Mei, he attacked Qin prefecture and won substantial merit.

sentences.zh: 及從楊業，為遼兵所圍，親射殺數十人，矢盡，張空弮又擊殺數人，遂遇害。

translations.literal: When he followed Yang Ye he was surrounded by Liao troops, personally shot and killed several tens of men, and when his arrows were exhausted he drew the empty bow and again killed several men before meeting his death.
translations.idiomatic: With Yang Ye he was surrounded by Liao troops, shot down dozens of the enemy, and when his arrows ran out killed several more with an empty bow before he fell.

sentences.zh: 年七十三。

translations.literal: He was seventy-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 擢其子文晟供奉官、文昱殿直。

translations.literal: His sons Wensheng and Wenyu were promoted to palace attendant and palace guard respectively.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Wensheng and Wenyu were made palace attendant and palace guard.

sentences.zh: 荊罕儒

translations.literal: Jing Hanru
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hanru

sentences.zh: 荊罕儒，冀州信都人。

translations.literal: Jing Hanru was a native of Xindu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Hanru came from Xindu in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 父基，王屋令。

translations.literal: His father Ji was magistrate of Wangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji had been magistrate of Wangwu.

sentences.zh: 罕儒少無賴，與趙鳳、張輦為群盜。

translations.literal: When young Hanru was unruly and together with Zhao Feng and Zhang Nian formed a band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hanru was a ruffian who ran with Zhao Feng and Zhang Nian as bandits.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，相率詣范陽，委質燕王趙延壽，得掌親兵。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin they led one another to Fanyang and submitted to Yan Prince Zhao Yanshou, obtaining command of his personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's Tianfu era they went to Fanyang and entered the service of Zhao Yanshou, prince of Yan, commanding his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 開運末，延壽從契丹主德光入汴，署罕儒密州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun Yanshou followed the Khitan lord Deguang into Bian and appointed Hanru prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyun Yanshou followed the Khitan emperor Deguang into Bian and made Hanru prefect of Mi.

sentences.zh: 漢初，改山南東道行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the early Han he was changed to campaigning marshal of the Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han he was made campaigning marshal of the Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，為率府率，奉朝請，貧不能振。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun he was a rate-house guard and court attendant, too poor to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Later Zhou Guangshun he was a rate-house guard and court attendant, too poor to live on his salary.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，世宗戰高平，戮不用命者，因求驍勇士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande the Shizong fought at Gaoping, executed those who disobeyed orders, and therefore sought fierce brave men.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande Emperor Shizong fought at Gaoping, executed men who disobeyed orders, and sought fierce warriors.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人李延傑以罕儒聞，即召赴行在，命為招收都指揮使。

translations.literal: Palace envoy Li Yanjie reported Hanru by name; he was at once summoned to the imperial camp and appointed overall recruitment commander.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoy Li Yanjie named Hanru; he was summoned to the imperial camp and made overall recruitment commander.

sentences.zh: 會徵太原，命罕儒率步卒三千先入敵境。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was to be attacked he ordered Hanru to lead three thousand foot soldiers to enter the enemy territory first.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan was attacked he ordered Hanru to lead three thousand foot soldiers into enemy territory first.

sentences.zh: 罕儒令人負束芻徑趨太原城，焚其東門。

translations.literal: Hanru had men carry bundles of straw and rush straight for Taiyuan city, burning its eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru had men carry bundles of straw straight to Taiyuan and burn the eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 擢為控鶴弩手、大劍直都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to crossbowman of the Crane Control Guard and overall commander of the Great Sword Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to crossbowman of the Crane Control Guard and commander of the Great Sword Guard.

sentences.zh: 從平淮南，領光州刺史，改泰州，為下蔡守禦都指揮使兼舒、蘄二州招安巡檢使。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Huainan he held Guang prefecture, was changed to Taizhou, and was made overall defense commander of Xiaocai and concurrently recruitment inspector of Shu and Qi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huainan campaign he governed Guang, then Taizhou, and commanded the defense of Xiaocai while inspecting Shu and Qi.

sentences.zh: 四年，泰州初下，真拜刺史兼海陵、鹽城兩監屯田使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Taizhou was first taken, he was formally appointed prefect and concurrently commissioner of the Hailing and Yancheng salt-field garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Taizhou fell, he was formally made prefect and commissioner of the Hailing and Yancheng salt garrisons.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，世宗幸泰州，以罕儒為團練使，賜金帶、銀器、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year the Shizong visited Taizhou, made Hanru regimental trainer, and granted a gold belt, silver vessels, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Shizong visited Taizhou, made Hanru regimental trainer, and gave him a gold belt, silver vessels, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 六年春，軍吏耆艾詣闕請留，恭帝詔褒之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year army officers and elders of the prefecture went to court requesting he remain; Emperor Gong issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year local officers and elders petitioned the court to keep him; Emperor Gong praised him in an edict.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，升鄭州防禦，以罕儒為使，改晉州兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong Zhengzhou defense was raised in rank and Hanru was made commissioner; he was changed to military commissioner of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianlong he was made defense commissioner of Zheng, then military commissioner of Jin.

sentences.zh: 罕儒恃勇輕敵，嘗率騎深入晉境，人多閉壁不出，虜獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Hanru relied on his courage and despised the enemy; he often led cavalry deep into Jin territory while many people shut their walls and did not come out, and he captured booty in great number.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru was reckless and overbold, often raiding deep into Jin territory while the people barricaded themselves; he returned with rich booty.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，復領千餘騎抵汾州城下，焚其草市，案兵以退。

translations.literal: That winter he again led more than a thousand cavalry to Fenzhou below the walls, burned its market outside the walls, and withdrew with his army in array.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he led more than a thousand horsemen to Fenzhou, burned the market outside the walls, and withdrew in good order.

sentences.zh: 夕次京土原，劉鈞遣大將郝貴超領萬餘眾襲罕儒，黎明及之。

translations.literal: At evening he halted at Jingtu Plain; Liu Jun sent the great general Hao Guichao leading more than ten thousand men to strike Hanru, and at dawn they reached him.
translations.idiomatic: He camped that night on Jingtu Plain; Liu Jun sent General Hao Guichao with more than ten thousand men, who caught him at dawn.

sentences.zh: 罕儒遣都監、氈毯副使閻彥進分兵以禦貴超。

translations.literal: Hanru sent the army supervisor and felt-blanket vice commissioner Yan Yanjin to divide troops to resist Guichao.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru sent his army supervisor Yan Yanjin to split the force and hold off Guichao.

sentences.zh: 罕儒錦袍裹甲據胡床享士，方割羊臂臑以啖，聞彥進小卻，即上馬麾兵徑犯賊鋒。

translations.literal: Hanru in brocade robe wrapped in armor sat on a camp chair treating his men, just cutting lamb shoulder to eat, when he heard Yanjin had given ground slightly; he at once mounted his horse and waved the army straight against the enemy vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in brocade over his armor, Hanru sat on a camp stool feasting on lamb when he heard Yanjin was giving ground; he mounted at once and charged straight into the enemy van.

sentences.zh: 并人攢戈舂之，罕儒猶格鬥，手殺十數人，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The Bing men piled spears and pounded him; Hanru still fought hand to hand, personally killing more than ten men, and thereupon met his death.
translations.idiomatic: The Bing troops battered him with spears, yet he fought on and killed more than ten before he fell.

sentences.zh: 劉鈞素畏罕儒之勇，常欲生致，及聞其死，求殺罕儒者戮之。

translations.literal: Liu Jun had long feared Hanru's courage and often wished to take him alive; when he heard of his death he sought those who had killed Hanru and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun had long feared Hanru and wanted him alive; when he heard of his death he had the killers executed.

sentences.zh: 太祖痛惜不已，擢其子守勳為西京武德副使。

translations.literal: The Taizu grieved deeply without end and promoted his son Shouxun to deputy commissioner of the Western Capital Wude.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu mourned him deeply and promoted his son Shouxun to deputy commissioner of the Western Capital Wude.

sentences.zh: 因索京土原之不效命者，黜慈州團練使王繼勳為率府率，閻彥進為殿直，斬其部下龍捷指揮使石進德等二十九人。

translations.literal: He therefore demanded those at Jingtu Plain who had not obeyed orders: demoted Cizhou regimental trainer Wang Jixun to rate-house guard, Yan Yanjin to palace guard, and beheaded his subordinate Dragon Swift commander Shi Jinde and twenty-nine others.
translations.idiomatic: He punished those who had failed at Jingtu Plain: Wang Jixun was demoted, Yan Yanjin reduced to palace guard, and twenty-nine subordinates including commander Shi Jinde were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 罕儒輕財好施。

translations.literal: Hanru was light with wealth and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru was generous and free with his wealth.

sentences.zh: 在泰州，有煮海之利，歲入鉅萬，詔聽十收其八，用猶不足。

translations.literal: At Taizhou he had the profit of boiling sea salt and yearly income of tens of thousands; an edict permitted him to keep eight tenths of ten, yet his use was still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizhou the salt monopoly brought him tens of thousands a year; the court let him keep eight-tenths, yet he still spent more than he had.

sentences.zh: 家財入有籍，出不問其數。

translations.literal: Household wealth had registers for what came in but for what went out he did not inquire into the number.
translations.idiomatic: His household kept accounts of income but never tracked what he gave away.

sentences.zh: 有供奉官張奉珪使泰州，自言後唐張承業之子。

translations.literal: There was a palace attendant Zhang Fenggui sent to Taizhou who declared himself the son of Later Tang's Zhang Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant named Zhang Fenggui came to Taizhou claiming to be the son of Later Tang's Zhang Chengye.

sentences.zh: 罕儒曰：「我生平聞張特進名，幸而識其子。」

translations.literal: Hanru said: "All my life I have heard the name of Special Advance Zhang; it is fortunate to know his son."
translations.idiomatic: Hanru said, "All my life I have revered Special Advance Zhang; how fortunate to meet his son."

sentences.zh: 厚加禮待，遺錢五十萬，米千斛。

translations.literal: He treated him with thick courtesy and sent him five hundred thousand in cash and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He honored him lavishly and gave him five hundred thousand cash and a thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 罕儒雖不知書，好禮接儒士。

translations.literal: Although Hanru did not know books he was fond of courtesy in receiving Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Though illiterate, Hanru treated scholars with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 進士趙保雍登科覆落，客遊海陵。

translations.literal: The advanced scholar Zhao Baoyong passed the examinations but was struck from the rolls and traveled as a guest at Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: The jinshi Zhao Baoyong had passed the examinations but was struck from the rolls and was traveling at Hailing.

sentences.zh: 罕儒問其所欲，保雍以將歸京師，且言緣江榷務以絲易茗有厚利。

translations.literal: Hanru asked what he desired; Baoyong said he was about to return to the capital and added that along the Yangzi monopoly trade exchanging silk for tea had thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru asked what he needed; Baoyong said he was returning to the capital and that trading silk for tea along the Yangzi could be highly profitable.

sentences.zh: 罕儒立召主藏奴，令籍藏中絲，得四千餘兩，盡以與之。

translations.literal: Hanru at once summoned the chief storekeeper, ordered the silk in the treasury recorded, obtained more than four thousand liang, and gave it all to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru summoned his chief steward, counted more than four thousand liang of silk in the treasury, and gave it all to him.

sentences.zh: 然好勇善戰，不顧勝負。

translations.literal: Yet he loved courage and was skilled in battle, heedless of victory or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved battle and cared nothing for victory or defeat.

sentences.zh: 常欲削平太原，志未果而及於敗，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: He often wished to level Taiyuan; his ambition was not fulfilled before he met defeat, and all men regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He longed to conquer Taiyuan but died before he could; all who knew him mourned it.

sentences.zh: 罕儒兄延福。

translations.literal: Hanru's elder brother Yanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru's elder brother Yanfu.

sentences.zh: 延福孫嗣。

translations.literal: Yanfu's grandson Si.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfu's grandson Si.

sentences.zh: 從孫 嗣

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Si
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew: Yang Si

sentences.zh: 嗣，乾德初，應募為控鶴卒，從李繼勳討河東。

translations.literal: Si, at the beginning of Qiande, answered the recruitment call as a Crane Control guardsman and followed Li Jixun in campaigning against Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Si enlisted as a Crane Control guardsman in early Qiande and followed Li Jixun against Hedong.

sentences.zh: 繼勳擇悍勇百人，間道截洛陽砦。

translations.literal: Jixun chose a hundred fierce brave men to take a bypath and cut off the Luoyang stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun picked a hundred fierce men to take a hidden route and cut off the Luoyang stockade.

sentences.zh: 嗣出行間請行，手斬五十餘級，賊焚砦宵遁。

translations.literal: Si went out between the ranks and requested to go, with his own hand beheading more than fifty heads; the bandits burned the stockade and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Si stepped forward to volunteer, cut down more than fifty of the enemy, and the rebels burned the stockade and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 進薄汾河，賊將楊業扼橋路，嗣與眾轉戰，賊退逾橋。

translations.literal: Pressing close to the Fen River, the bandit general Yang Ye held the bridge road; Si with the masses fought in turn and the bandits retreated across the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the Fen River, the enemy general Yang Ye held the bridge; Si fought through the engagement until the enemy retreated across the bridge.

sentences.zh: 殺業所部兵千計，射中業從騎，獲旗鼓鎧甲甚眾，業退保城。

translations.literal: He killed more than a thousand of Ye's troops, shot Ye's mounted follower, and captured banners, drums, armor, and mail in great number; Ye withdrew to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: He killed more than a thousand of Yang Ye's men, shot down one of his mounted followers, and captured many banners, drums, and armor before Yang Ye withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 進焚南門，奪羊馬城，矢集於面。

translations.literal: Advancing he burned the southern gate and seized the sheep-and-horse wall; arrows clustered on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, burned the southern gate, and took the sheep-and-horse wall while arrows rained on his face.

sentences.zh: 賊數千夜來薄砦，繼勳選勇敢五百人接戰，而嗣為冠。

translations.literal: Several thousand bandits came by night to press the stockade; Jixun chose five hundred brave men to give battle, and Si was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of enemy came by night against the stockade; Jixun chose five hundred brave men to fight, with Si in the lead.

sentences.zh: 及旦，戰數合，多所斬馘。

translations.literal: By dawn they had fought several engagements and beheaded and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn they had fought several rounds and taken many heads.

sentences.zh: 從太祖征太原，賊來拒，焚洞子。

translations.literal: Following the Taizu in campaigning against Taiyuan, when bandits came to resist they burned the siege shelters.
translations.idiomatic: Following Taizu against Taiyuan, when the enemy resisted they burned the siege works.

sentences.zh: 遣殿前楊信領百人援之，嗣預焉，率先陷陣。

translations.literal: He sent Hall Front Yang Xin leading a hundred men to reinforce; Si was among them and was first to break the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Yang Xin of the Hall Front with a hundred men; Si was among them and was first through the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 召見，補御龍直。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience he was appointed Imperial Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he was made an Imperial Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，三遷至天武軍校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was three times promoted to captain of the Celestial Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he rose three ranks to captain of the Celestial Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 太宗再征太原，嗣自陳願率一隊先登，命主城西洞子。

translations.literal: When the Taizong again campaigned against Taiyuan, Si volunteered to lead a unit to ascend first and was ordered to command the western siege shelters of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong again attacked Taiyuan, Si volunteered to lead the first assault and was put in charge of the western siege works.

sentences.zh: 車駕巡師，嗣登城，手刃數賊，足貫雙箭，中手炮，折二齒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage inspected the army, Si ascended the wall, with his own hand killed several bandits, had both feet pierced by two arrows, was struck on the hand by a catapult stone, and two teeth were broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reviewed the army, Si climbed the wall, killed several of the enemy, took two arrows through both feet, a catapult stone on the hand, and broke two teeth.

sentences.zh: 太宗見之，亟召賜錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: When the Taizong saw it he urgently summoned and granted brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw this and at once summoned him, granting a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 從征幽州，隸殿前崔翰，斬三十級，補龍猛副指揮使。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Youzhou he was under Hall Front Cui Han, beheaded thirty ranks, and was appointed deputy commander of the Dragon Fierce Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the Youzhou campaign he served under Cui Han, took thirty heads, and was made deputy commander of the Dragon Fierce Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，契丹侵雄州，據龍灣堤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Khitan invaded Xiongzhou and held the Longwan embankment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Khitan invaded Xiongzhou and held the Longwan embankment.

sentences.zh: 嗣隸袁繼忠，繼忠令率千兵力戰奪路。

translations.literal: Si was under Yuan Jizhong; Jizhong ordered him to lead a thousand men to fight fiercely and seize the road.
translations.idiomatic: Si served under Yuan Jizhong, who ordered him to lead a thousand men in a fierce fight to break through.

sentences.zh: 內侍有至州閱城壘者，出郛外，敵進圍之，亟出兵接戰，十數合，斬騎卒七百餘。

translations.literal: A palace attendant came to the prefecture to inspect the ramparts; going outside the outer wall he was surrounded by advancing enemy; Si urgently led troops out to meet the battle, fought more than ten engagements, and beheaded more than seven hundred mounted soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant came to inspect the fortifications, went outside the wall, and was surrounded by the enemy; Si rushed out to fight, and in more than ten engagements cut down over seven hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 嗣軍夜相失，在古城莊外，三鼓突敵圍，壁于莫州城下，又領百人斧敵望櫓，斬五十級。

translations.literal: Si's army lost one another in the night; outside Gucheng village at the third watch he burst through the enemy encirclement, fortified below Mozhou walls, and again led a hundred men to axe the enemy watchtower, beheading fifty ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Si's troops were scattered by night; at the third watch outside Gucheng village he broke through the encirclement, held below Mozhou, and led a hundred men to chop down an enemy watchtower, taking fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 敵為橋界河，將遁，嗣邀擊之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The enemy made a bridge across the river and were about to flee; Si intercepted and struck them, killing and capturing a great number.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy bridged the river to escape; Si intercepted them and killed or captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 六年，從崔彥進捍契丹於靜戎北，砦於慎興口。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Cui Yanjin in resisting the Khitan north of Jingrong, encamping at Shenxingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Cui Yanjin against the Khitan north of Jingrong and camped at Shenxingkou.

sentences.zh: 彥進遣嗣率所部度河，與契丹戰，敗之，追奔二十餘里。

translations.literal: Yanjin sent Si to lead his command across the river to fight the Khitan, defeated them, and pursued the rout more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin sent Si across the river; he defeated the Khitan and pursued them more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 八年，李繼遷寇邊，嗣從袁繼忠、田欽祚戍三叉口，為前鋒，斬賊千餘，追之，獲牛羊、鎧甲、弓矢數千計。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Li Jiqian raided the frontier; Si followed Yuan Jizhong and Tian Qinzu in garrisoning Sanchakou as vanguard, beheaded more than a thousand bandits, pursued them, and obtained cattle, sheep, armor, bows, and arrows numbering several thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Li Jiqian raided the border, Si served under Yuan Jizhong and Tian Qinzu at Sanchakou as vanguard, killed more than a thousand rebels, and captured thousands of cattle, sheep, arms, and bows.

sentences.zh: 進至萬井口、狐路谷，餘賊復來請戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to Wanjingkou and Hulu Valley, the remaining bandits again came to request battle.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Wanjingkou and Hulu Valley, the remaining enemy came out to fight again.

sentences.zh: 初以雄武千人為後殿，為賊所掩。

translations.literal: At first a thousand men of the Fierce Martial Army were made rear guard and were masked by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand Fierce Martial troops formed the rear guard and were ambushed.

sentences.zh: 繼忠命嗣援之，凡數戰，始與雄武合隊，因列陣格鬥，復奪人馬七百餘。

translations.literal: Jizhong ordered Si to reinforce them; after several battles they at last joined the Fierce Martial company, arrayed formations and fought hand to hand, and again recovered more than seven hundred men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong sent Si to rescue them; after several fights they rejoined the Fierce Martial detachment, formed ranks, and recovered more than seven hundred men and horses.

sentences.zh: 欽祚夜還，依山為營，賊亦砦其下。

translations.literal: Qinzu returned by night and made camp leaning on the mountain; the bandits also stockaded below them.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzu withdrew by night and camped on the mountainside while the enemy camped below.

sentences.zh: 募勁卒五十往襲之，嗣為其帥。

translations.literal: He recruited fifty fierce soldiers to strike them by night, with Si as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fifty picked men for a night attack, with Si in command.

sentences.zh: 抵賊所，刺殺百餘人，焚其砦而還，詔賜錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: Reaching the enemy position they stabbed and killed more than a hundred men, burned their stockade and returned; an edict granted brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: They reached the enemy camp, killed more than a hundred, burned the stockade, and returned; the court granted Si a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，從田重進、譚延美率師入遼境，疾戰飛狐口，遼師不利。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he followed Tian Chongjin and Tan Yanmei in leading troops into Liao territory, fighting fiercely at Feihukou where the Liao army met with misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he followed Tian Chongjin and Tan Yanmei into Liao territory and fought fiercely at Feihukou, where the Liao army was beaten.

sentences.zh: 重進引全師合擊，遼騎引去。

translations.literal: Chongjin led the full army in combined attack and the Liao horsemen withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin brought the full army to bear and the Liao cavalry withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進至飛狐城北，遼將大鵬翼率眾復至。

translations.literal: Advancing to north of Feihu city, the Liao general Dapengyi led the masses and came again.
translations.idiomatic: As they reached north of Feihu city, the Liao general Dapengyi returned with a large force.

sentences.zh: 重進陣壓東偏，數戰不勝，命嗣出西偏，麾兵薄山崖，以短兵接戰。

translations.literal: Chongjin arrayed his force pressing the eastern wing; after several battles without victory he ordered Si out on the western wing, waving troops close to the mountain cliff to join battle with short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin attacked from the east without success and sent Si to the western flank to drive his men along the cliff and fight at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 遼兵敗，投崖而下，手斬百餘級。

translations.literal: The Liao soldiers were defeated and threw themselves off the cliff; with his own hand he beheaded more than a hundred ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao troops broke and hurled themselves off the cliff; Si personally took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 散卒千餘在野，嗣呵止之，悉斷弦折筈來降，追至河槽，復擊退。

translations.literal: More than a thousand scattered soldiers were in the wild; Si shouted to stop them, all broke their bowstrings and snapped their arrow shafts and came to surrender; pursuing to the river channel he again struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand stragglers were in the open; Si halted them, and they broke their bows and surrendered; pursuing to the riverbed he drove the rest back.

sentences.zh: 餘眾屯土嶺，裨將黃明與戰不勝，將退，嗣謂之曰：「汝且頓兵於此，為我聲援，我當奪此嶺。」

translations.literal: The remaining masses encamped on an earthen ridge; vice-general Huang Ming fought without victory and was about to withdraw; Si said to him: "You for the moment hold your troops here as my supporting shout; I shall seize this ridge."
translations.idiomatic: The rest held an earthen ridge; Vice-General Huang Ming was losing and about to retreat when Si told him, "Hold here as my reserve—I will take that ridge."

sentences.zh: 遂力戰，追奔五十餘里，抵倉頭而還。

translations.literal: He thereupon fought with all his strength, pursued the rout more than fifty li, reached Cangtou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on, pursued the enemy more than fifty li to Cangtou, and returned.

sentences.zh: 又領招收卒千人，克倉頭、小治二砦。

translations.literal: He again led a thousand recruitment soldiers and captured the stockades of Cangtou and Xiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He led a thousand recruits and took the stockades at Cangtou and Xiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 黃明與戰，克直谷砦，命嗣屯焉。

translations.literal: Huang Ming fought and captured Zhigu stockade; he ordered Si to encamp there.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ming captured Zhigu stockade and left Si to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 數日，遼人復致師，重進與戰，奔突往來，大軍頗擾。

translations.literal: Several days later the Liao men again brought troops; Chongjin fought them, charging back and forth, and the great army was considerably disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the Liao returned; Chongjin fought them in confused charges that threw the main army into disorder.

sentences.zh: 重進召嗣合戰，悉走之，奪礮具、鎧胄。

translations.literal: Chongjin summoned Si to join battle and completely drove them off, seizing artillery equipment and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin called Si into the fight; together they routed the enemy and seized cannon and armor.

sentences.zh: 賊乘夜復圍直谷、石門二砦，重進遣嗣以精兵五百濟之，嗣曰：「敵二萬餘，今援師甚寡，難以解圍。」

translations.literal: The bandits by night again surrounded the Zhigu and Shimen stockades; Chongjin sent Si with five hundred elite troops to relieve them; Si said: "The enemy are more than twenty thousand; now the relief force is very few and hard pressed to lift the siege."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy surrounded Zhigu and Shimen by night; Chongjin sent Si with five hundred elite troops, but Si said, "The enemy number more than twenty thousand—five hundred cannot break a siege."

sentences.zh: 重進頗憂之。

translations.literal: Chongjin was quite worried.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 嗣曰：「譚師屯小治，綰兵二千，願間道以往，邀其策應。」

translations.literal: Si said: "Master Tan is encamped at Xiaozhi with two thousand troops drawn together; I wish to go by a hidden route and intercept their coordinated response."
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "Tan Yanmei holds Xiaozhi with two thousand men—I will take a hidden route and cut off their coordination."

sentences.zh: 中夜，匹馬詣延美，延美曰：「敵勢若此，何可解也？」

translations.literal: At midnight he went alone on horseback to Yanmei; Yanmei said: "The enemy situation is like this—how can it be resolved?"
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he rode alone to Yanmei, who said, "With the enemy in this strength, how can we save them?"

sentences.zh: 嗣曰：「請移全軍就平川，植旗立隊，別擇三二百人張白旗於道側。

translations.literal: Si said: "Please move the full army to level ground, plant flags and establish ranks, and separately choose two or three hundred men to stretch white flags along the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "Move your whole force to open ground, form ranks with banners, and post two or three hundred men with white flags along the road.

sentences.zh: 彼見旗幟綿亙遠甚，謂大軍繼至，嗣自以所部五百疾驅往鬥，必克其砦。」

translations.literal: When they see banners stretching far in the distance they will think the great army has followed close behind; I with the five hundred under my command will gallop to fight and surely capture their stockade."
translations.idiomatic: When they see banners stretching far along the road they will think a great army is coming; I will charge with my five hundred and take their camp."

sentences.zh: 延美許焉。

translations.literal: Yanmei agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmei agreed.

sentences.zh: 一日凡五七戰，遼兵遂引去，咸如嗣所料。

translations.literal: In one day they fought five or seven battles and the Liao soldiers thereupon withdrew, all as Si had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: They fought five or seven engagements in a day and the Liao withdrew, exactly as Si had predicted.

sentences.zh: 蔚州之降也，重進先命嗣率勇士數十人縋入，見守將，得其實狀。

translations.literal: When Yu prefecture surrendered, Chongjin first ordered Si to lead several tens of brave men to lower themselves on ropes into the city, see the defending general, and learn the true situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunzhou was to surrender, Chongjin first sent Si with dozens of brave men over the wall to learn the defenders' true intentions.

sentences.zh: 翌日，將受降，而敵反拒大軍所出之路，遂與鬥，殺傷甚眾，屢縋入城，取守將之歸服者。

translations.literal: The next day they were to accept the surrender, but the enemy instead blocked the route by which the great army was to exit, and therefore fought; casualties were very numerous; repeatedly lowering on ropes into the city they took those of the defending generals who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, as surrender was to be accepted, the enemy blocked the army's exit and heavy fighting ensued; Si repeatedly entered the city by rope to bring out those commanders who had submitted.

sentences.zh: 重進之壘，糧運頗乏，嗣遣降卒輦州廩濟之。

translations.literal: Chongjin's stockade was quite short of grain transport; Si sent surrendered soldiers to cart prefectural granaries to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin's camp was short of supplies; Si sent surrendered troops to haul grain from the prefectural stores.

sentences.zh: 遼援兵大至，副都指揮使江謙妄言惑眾，嗣即斬之。

translations.literal: Liao relief troops came in great force; deputy overall commander Jiang Qian spoke reckless words to confuse the masses, and Si at once beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liao reinforcements arrived in force; Deputy Commander Jiang Qian spread panic, and Si beheaded him at once.

sentences.zh: 悉收兵斂輜重還重進砦，與遼人轉戰。

translations.literal: He gathered all troops, collected baggage and heavy equipment, returned to Chongjin's stockade, and fought in turn with the Liao men.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the army, collected baggage, fell back to Chongjin's camp, and fought the Liao in successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 時軍校五人，其四悉鬥死，至大嶺，嗣與戰，敗走之。

translations.literal: At that time five army officers—four of them all fought and died—reaching Great Ridge, Si fought and defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Of five officers in the fight four died; at Great Ridge Si fought and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 師還，太宗引見便殿，重進言其有勞，補本軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When the army returned the Taizong received him in audience at the side hall; Chongjin said he had merit and he was appointed chief adjutant of his army.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return Taizong received him in the side hall; Chongjin commended his service and he was made chief adjutant of his command.

sentences.zh: 又從李繼隆禦敵于北平砦，將赴蒲城，道遇敵，疾戰，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He again followed Li Jilong in resisting the enemy at Beiping stockade; about to go to Pucheng they met enemy on the road, fought fiercely, and captured prisoners in great number.
