translations.idiomatic: He again followed Li Jilong at Beiping stockade; marching toward Pucheng they met the enemy, fought fiercely, and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 又戰於鸞女祠，繼隆遣步卒二千，伏定州古城，為敵所攻，命嗣援之。

translations.literal: They again fought at Luannü Shrine; Jilong sent two thousand foot soldiers to lie in ambush at the ancient city of Dingzhou, were attacked by the enemy, and ordered Si to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again at Luannü Shrine; Jilong had two thousand foot soldiers ambush at Dingzhou's old city, and when they were attacked sent Si to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 至唐河橋，嗣扼橋路出戰，解敵圍數重，與伏兵合，分為三隊，背水為陣。

translations.literal: Reaching Tanghe Bridge, Si held the bridge route and went out to fight, broke several layers of enemy encirclement, joined the ambush troops, and divided into three companies arrayed with their backs to the water.
translations.idiomatic: At Tanghe Bridge Si held the crossing, broke through several encirclements, joined the ambush force, and formed three companies with their backs to the water.

sentences.zh: 敵將于越率騎百餘隊臨烽臺求戰，嗣整兵與戰，數合，得與繼隆會，又陣於東偏，大敗之。

translations.literal: The enemy general Yuyue led more than a hundred companies of cavalry to the beacon tower seeking battle; Si arrayed troops and fought, after several engagements was able to join Jilong, again arrayed on the eastern wing, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Yuyue brought more than a hundred cavalry companies to challenge them at the beacon tower; after several rounds Si joined Jilong on the eastern wing and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 繼隆以聞，詔嘉獎之，遷本軍都指揮使，領澄州刺史。

translations.literal: Jilong reported it; an edict praised and rewarded him, and he was transferred to overall commander of his army and held Cheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong reported the victory; the court praised and rewarded him and made him overall commander of his army and prefect of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，加御前忠佐馬步軍頭、屯定州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was added as head of the Loyal Attendant Horse and Foot Army before the throne and encamped at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was made head of the Loyal Attendant Horse and Foot Guard before the throne and stationed at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼人入侵，隸范廷召，提偏師捍遼兵於嘉山。

translations.literal: When the Liao invaded he was under Fan Tingzhao and led a separate column to resist Liao troops at Jia Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao invaded he served under Fan Tingzhao and led a detached force against them at Jia Mountain.

sentences.zh: 廷召徙高陽，命嗣以兵二千為殿。

translations.literal: Tingzhao moved to Gaoyang and ordered Si with two thousand troops as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao moved to Gaoyang and left Si with two thousand men as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 過平敵城，遼眾十餘萬來，嗣屢出戰。

translations.literal: Passing Pingdi city, Liao masses of more than one hundred thousand came; Si repeatedly went out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Pingdi, more than a hundred thousand Liao troops came up and Si fought them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 及桑贊、秦翰來援，夜二鼓，敵再至，嗣曰：「彼不利夜戰，我當破其砦，以趣大軍。」

translations.literal: When Sang Zan and Qin Han came to relieve, at the second watch of night the enemy came again; Si said: "They are not suited to night battle; we ought to break their stockade and hurry to the great army."
translations.idiomatic: When Sang Zan and Qin Han arrived, the enemy attacked again at the second watch; Si said, "They dislike night fighting—we should break their camp and rejoin the main force."

sentences.zh: 即與贊、翰合勢，戒所部望敵炬火多處並力衝之，詰旦，至瀛州。

translations.literal: He at once joined forces with Zan and Han, warned his command to strike with combined strength wherever enemy torch-fires were numerous, and by dawn reached Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sang Zan and Qin Han, ordered his men to strike wherever enemy fires clustered thickest, and by dawn reached Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，加領本州團練使，出為郎山路都巡檢使，破敵砦于蒲陰，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he was added as regimental trainer of his home prefecture, went out as overall inspector of the Langshan route, broke an enemy stockade at Puyin, and captured prisoners in great number.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was made regimental trainer of his home prefecture and overall inspector of the Langshan route, stormed an enemy camp at Puyin, and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 四年，命嗣領萬人斷西山路。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to lead ten thousand men to cut the western mountain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was ordered to lead ten thousand men to block the western mountain route.

sentences.zh: 會敵遽至，大兵不及進而止。

translations.literal: The enemy suddenly arrived and the great army had no time to advance and halted.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came up suddenly and the main army could not advance in time and halted.

sentences.zh: 五年，真拜蔡州團練使、趙州部署。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was formally appointed regimental trainer of Caizhou and deployment commander of Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was formally made regimental trainer of Cai and deployment commander of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 逾年，徙滄州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遼人入侵，命率所部自齊州抵淄、青警備。

translations.literal: That winter the Liao invaded; he was ordered to lead his command from Qizhou to reach Zi and Qing for alert defense.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Liao invaded, he was ordered to lead his troops from Qizhou to guard Zi and Qing.

sentences.zh: 景德初，又命與劉漢凝、田思明率兵至冀州防邊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was again ordered with Liu Hanning and Tian Siming to lead troops to Jizhou to defend the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he was again ordered with Liu Hanning and Tian Siming to Jizhou for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 俄赴澶州行在所。

translations.literal: Soon he went to the mobile court at Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to the mobile court at Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 會遼人請和，復遣還任。

translations.literal: When the Liao requested peace he was again sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao sued for peace he was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 歷鄆州、鳳翔、永興部署。

translations.literal: He successively held deployment commands at Yunzhou, Fengxiang, and Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: He held deployment commands at Yun, Fengxiang, and Yongxing in succession.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸亳州，留為舊城內同都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Bozhou he was left as co-overall inspector within the old city walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Bozhou he was left as co-overall inspector of the old city.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，改虢州防禦使、邠甯環慶副部署，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was changed to defense commissioner of Guo and deputy deployment of Binning, Huanqing, and Ring; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was made defense commissioner of Guo and deputy commander of Binning, Huan, and Qing, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 嗣起行間，以勞居方面，經百五十餘戰，歿。

translations.literal: Si rose from the ranks; through merit he held a frontier post; he passed through more than one hundred fifty battles and died.
translations.idiomatic: Si rose from the ranks, earned a frontier command through merit, fought in more than one hundred fifty battles, and died.

sentences.zh: 兄子信、貴，並為左侍禁，貴至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His nephews Xin and Gui were both Left Attendant Guards; Gui rose to Inner Hall Honored Ban.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Xin and Gui were both Left Attendant Guards; Gui rose to Inner Hall Honored Ban.

sentences.zh: 曹光實

translations.literal: Cao Guangshi
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guangshi

sentences.zh: 曹光實，雅州百丈人。

translations.literal: Cao Guangshi was a native of Baizhang in Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Guangshi came from Baizhang in Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父疇，為蜀靜南軍使，控扼邛崍，以捍蠻夷。

translations.literal: His father Chou was military commissioner of the Jingnan Army of Shu, controlling Qionglai to resist the Man barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chou had been Shu's Jingnan Army commissioner, holding Qionglai against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 光實少武勇，有膽氣，輕財好施，不事細行，意豁如也。

translations.literal: When young Guangshi was martial and brave, had courage and spirit, was light with wealth and fond of giving, did not attend to minor conduct, and his intent was open and free.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Guangshi was brave and generous, careless of small proprieties, and open-hearted.

sentences.zh: 疇卒，光實嗣職，遷永平軍節度管內捕盜游奕使。

translations.literal: When Chou died Guangshi succeeded to the post and was transferred to roaming bandit-catcher of the Yongping Army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou died Guangshi succeeded him and was made roaming bandit-catcher of the Yongping circuit.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，太祖命王全斌等平蜀。

translations.literal: In Qiande the Taizu ordered Wang Quanbin and others to pacify Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande Taizu ordered Wang Quanbin and others to pacify Shu.

sentences.zh: 俄而盜賊群起，夷人張忠樂者，嘗群行攻劫，且憾光實殺其徒黨，率眾數千，中夜奄至，環其居，鼓噪並進。

translations.literal: Before long bandits rose in groups; the barbarian Zhang Zhongle had often roamed in groups raiding, and because he resented Guangshi for killing his companions led several thousand men at midnight to come suddenly, surrounding his dwelling, drumming and shouting as they advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits rose everywhere; the barbarian Zhang Zhongle, resenting Guangshi for killing his followers, led thousands in a midnight assault on his home.

sentences.zh: 光實負其母，揮戈突圍以出，賊眾辟易不敢近，賊殺其族三百餘口。

translations.literal: Guangshi carried his mother on his back, waved a spear and burst through the encirclement; the bandit masses gave way and did not dare approach; the bandits killed more than three hundred of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi carried his mother on his back and fought through the encirclement; the enemy dared not close on him but slaughtered more than three hundred of his kin.

sentences.zh: 又發塚墓，壞其棺槨。

translations.literal: They also opened tombs and destroyed the coffins.
translations.idiomatic: They also opened the family tombs and destroyed the coffins.

sentences.zh: 光實詣全斌，具以事白，誓雪冤憤。

translations.literal: Guangshi went to Quanbin and reported the matter in full, vowing to wash away his bitter grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi went to Quanbin, reported everything, and vowed to avenge his family.

sentences.zh: 時蜀中諸郡未下，乃圖雅州地形要害，兼陳用兵攻取之策，請官軍先下之。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures of Shu had not yet fallen; he therefore mapped Yazhou's terrain and vital points, together presented a plan for using troops to attack and seize it, and requested that the government army first take it.
translations.idiomatic: Many Shu prefectures had not yet fallen; he mapped Yazhou's terrain, submitted a plan to take it, and asked the imperial army to strike there first.

sentences.zh: 全斌壯其志，令率兵先導，果克其城，獲忠樂而甘心焉。

translations.literal: Quanbin admired his resolve, ordered him to lead troops as guide, and indeed captured the city and obtained Zhongle to his heart's content.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin admired his spirit, had him lead the vanguard, took the city, and captured Zhongle.

sentences.zh: 全斌乃署光實為義軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Quanbin thereupon appointed Guangshi overall commander of the Loyal Army.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin then made Guangshi overall commander of the Loyal Army.

sentences.zh: 殘寇猶據沈黎，光實以所部盡平之。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits still held Shenli; Guangshi with his command completely pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits still held Shenli; Guangshi pacified them with his troops.

sentences.zh: 遂以光實知黎、雅二州兼都巡檢使，安集勞來，蠻族懷之。

translations.literal: He was then made to know Li and Ya prefectures and concurrently overall inspector, comforting and summoning the laboring people, and the barbarian tribes were attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Li and Ya and overall inspector, settled the people, and won the tribes' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，全斌遣入貢京師，遂言境內安乂，乞罷義軍歸農。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year Quanbin sent him to offer tribute at the capital and he thereupon said the territory within the borders was peaceful and secure and begged to disband the Loyal Army and return the people to farming.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year Quanbin sent him to court with tribute; he reported the region secure and asked to disband the Loyal Army so the people could farm.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，謂左右曰：「此蜀中傑俊也。」

translations.literal: The Taizu was pleased and said to those at his side: "This is a heroic talent of Shu."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was pleased and said to his attendants, "Here is a hero of Shu."

sentences.zh: 詔升殿，勞問久之，以為黎州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to ascend the hall; after long inquiry and consolation he was made prefect of Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the hall, questioned at length, and made prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，改唐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he was changed to Tang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he was transferred to Tang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及平交、廣，群盜未息，以光實為嶺南諸州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Jiao and Guang were pacified bandit groups had not yet ceased; Guangshi was made overall inspector of the various prefectures of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao and Guang were pacified, banditry continued; he was made overall inspector of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 既至，捕逐群盜，海隅以寧。

translations.literal: When he arrived he pursued bandits and the seacoast was thereby tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he hunted down bandits until the coast was quiet.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，就遷本州團練使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was concurrently promoted to regimental trainer of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to regimental trainer of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 車駕征河東，以光實知威勝軍事，令調軍食。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against Hedong, Guangshi was made to know Weisheng military affairs and ordered to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Hedong, Guangshi was put in charge of Weisheng and ordered to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 光實入告，願提一旅奮銳先登，帝曰：「資糧事重，亦足宣力也。」

translations.literal: Guangshi entered to report and wished to lead a column of fierce elite troops to ascend first; the emperor said: "The grain-supply affair is weighty and also sufficient to exert your strength."
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi asked to lead a picked column in the first assault; the emperor said, "Supplying the army is weighty work enough for your strength."

sentences.zh: 河東平，命為汾、遼、石、沁等州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Hedong was pacified he was appointed overall inspector of Fen, Liao, Shi, Qin, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong fell he was made overall inspector of Fen, Liao, Shi, Qin, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五年，改汝州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to regimental trainer of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made regimental trainer of Ru.

sentences.zh: 大軍北征，與潘美分道出雁門。

translations.literal: When the great army marched north he with Pan Mei divided forces and went out through Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he and Pan Mei marched out through Yanmen by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 光實為前鋒，遇敵迎擊，敗之，斬首數千級，優詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Guangshi was vanguard, met the enemy and gave battle, defeated them, beheaded several thousand ranks, and received a gracious edict of praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: As vanguard he met the enemy, defeated them, took several thousand heads, and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 李繼捧之入朝也，以光實為銀、夏、綏、麟、府、豐、宥州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Li Jibong came to court Guangshi was made overall inspector of Yin, Xia, Sui, Lin, Fu, Feng, and You prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jibong came to court, Guangshi was made overall inspector of Yin, Xia, Sui, Lin, Fu, Feng, and You.

sentences.zh: 繼捧弟繼遷逃入蕃落，為邊患，光實乘間掩襲至地斤澤，俘斬甚眾，破其族帳，獲繼遷母妻及牛羊萬計。

translations.literal: Jibong's younger brother Jiqian fled into the barbarian tribes and became a frontier trouble; Guangshi seized an opportunity for a masked strike to Dijin Marsh, beheaded and captured in great number, broke their tribal tents, and obtained Jiqian's mother, wife, cattle, and sheep numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jibong's brother Jiqian fled to the tribes and raided the border; Guangshi raided Dijin Marsh, killed and captured many, destroyed their camps, and seized Jiqian's mother, wife, and tens of thousands of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 繼遷僅免，使人紿光實曰：「我數奔北，勢窘不能自存矣，公許我降乎？」

translations.literal: Jiqian barely escaped and sent a man to deceive Guangshi saying: "I have several times fled north; my situation is desperate and I cannot preserve myself—will you, sir, permit me to surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian barely escaped and sent a messenger to deceive Guangshi: "I have fled again and again and cannot survive—will you accept my surrender?"

sentences.zh: 因致情款，陳甥舅之禮，期某日降于葭蘆川。

translations.literal: He thereby expressed sincere feeling and set forth nephew-and-uncle courtesy, fixing a certain day to surrender at Jialu River.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of kinship and promised to surrender on a set day at the Jialu River.

sentences.zh: 光實信之，且欲專其功，不與人謀。

translations.literal: Guangshi believed him and moreover wished to monopolize the merit, not consulting with others.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi believed him and, wanting the credit for himself, told no one.

sentences.zh: 及期，繼遷先設伏兵，令十數人近城迎致光實，光實從數百騎往赴之。

translations.literal: When the day arrived Jiqian first set ambush troops and ordered a dozen or so men near the city to welcome and conduct Guangshi; Guangshi followed with several hundred horsemen to go meet them.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Jiqian set an ambush and sent a dozen men to welcome him; Guangshi rode out with several hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 繼遷前導北行，將至其地，舉手麾鞭而伏兵應之，光實遂遇害，卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: Jiqian led the way north; when they were about to reach the place he raised his hand and waved his whip and the ambush troops responded; Guangshi thereupon met his death, dying aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian led him north; at the spot he signaled with his whip, the ambush sprang, and Guangshi was killed at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之驚悼，賵賻加等，以其子大理評事克讓為右贊善大夫，克恭為殿直。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was startled and mourned, increased funeral gifts by a grade, and made his son the Court of Judicial Review evaluator Kerang Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and Kejing a palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved, increased the funeral gifts, and made his sons Kerang and Kejing court officers.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，又錄克己為奉職，後至內殿承制；

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua Kerang was again enrolled as a court attendant, later reaching Inner Hall Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua Kerang was enrolled as a court attendant and later rose to Inner Hall Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 克廣至閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Kejing reached Pavilion Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kejing became a Pavilion Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從子克明。

translations.literal: Nephew Keming.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Cao Keming

sentences.zh: 從子 克明

translations.literal: Nephew: Keming
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Cao Keming

sentences.zh: 克明，字堯卿。

translations.literal: Keming, style name Yaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Keming, whose style name was Yaoqing,

sentences.zh: 既生，會敵攻百丈縣，父光遠遇害，姆抱克明匿葦蒲中得免。

translations.literal: When he was born the enemy attacked Baizhang county; his father Guangyuan met harm; the nurse carried Keming and hid him in reeds and rushes and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth the enemy attacked Baizhang; his father Guangyuan was killed, but his nurse hid the infant Keming in the reeds and he survived.

sentences.zh: 既長，喜兵法，善騎射，從父光實奇之。

translations.literal: When grown he loved military methods, was skilled at mounted archery, and his uncle Guangshi regarded him as remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he studied warfare and archery, and his uncle Guangshi took special notice of him.

sentences.zh: 補為衙內都虞候。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief adjutant within the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief adjutant of the yamen guard.

sentences.zh: 光實擊敵于葭蘆州，戰歿。

translations.literal: Guangshi attacked the enemy at Jialu prefecture and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi attacked the enemy at Jialu and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 克明時護輜重在後，聞光實死，懼軍亂，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Keming was then protecting baggage in the rear; hearing Guangshi had died he feared the army would fall into disorder and secretly did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Keming was guarding the baggage train; hearing of Guangshi's death he feared mutiny and kept the news secret.

sentences.zh: 陽令人西來傳光實命還軍銀州，而潛與僕張貴入敵中，獲光實屍以還，葬京師，由是顯名。

translations.literal: He pretended to have a man come from the west transmitting Guangshi's order to return the army to Yinzhou, while secretly with his servant Zhang Gui he entered among the enemy, obtained Guangshi's corpse and returned, buried it in the capital, and thereby gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned orders to withdraw to Yinzhou while slipping into enemy lines with his servant Zhang Gui to recover Guangshi's body, buried it in the capital, and won fame thereby.

sentences.zh: 初，蜀人留京師者禁不得還鄉里，克明以母老，間道歸。

translations.literal: At first Shu people remaining in the capital were forbidden to return to their home districts; Keming because his mother was old went home by a hidden route.
translations.idiomatic: Shu natives in the capital were forbidden to return home; Keming, whose mother was elderly, slipped back by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 李順反，聞克明將家子，且有名，欲脅以官。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled, hearing Keming was of a general's house and moreover had a name, they wished to coerce him into office.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled he sought Keming, a general's son with a reputation, hoping to force him into service.

sentences.zh: 克明攜母遁山谷，夜止神祠中，夢有人叱之起，既覺而去，賊果至。

translations.literal: Keming fled with his mother into the mountain valleys; at night they halted in a spirit shrine; he dreamed someone shouted at him to rise; when he awoke he left, and the bandits indeed came.
translations.idiomatic: Keming fled with his mother into the hills; camping in a shrine he dreamed a voice commanding him to rise—he left at once, and the rebels arrived as he had dreamed.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷雅州，克明募眾數萬人以迎王師，遂復名山、火井、夾江等九縣。

translations.literal: When the bandits took Yazhou, Keming recruited tens of thousands to welcome the imperial army and thereupon recovered the nine counties of Mingshan, Huojing, Jiajiang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized Yazhou, Keming raised tens of thousands to welcome the imperial army and recovered nine counties including Mingshan and Huojing.

sentences.zh: 分兵嘉、眉、邛三州，立七砦以邀賊。

translations.literal: He divided troops among Jia, Mei, and Qiong prefectures and established seven stockades to intercept the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He posted troops in Jia, Mei, and Qiong and built seven stockades to block the rebels.

sentences.zh: 復收雅州，斬六十餘人，賊將何承祿等走雲南。

translations.literal: He again recovered Yazhou, beheaded more than sixty men, and bandit generals He Chenglu and others fled to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Yazhou, executed more than sixty rebels, and drove He Chenglu and other rebel leaders into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，擢西頭供奉官、黎州兵馬監押。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was promoted to Western Head palace attendant and military supervisor of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was made Western Head palace attendant and military supervisor of Li.

sentences.zh: 以餘寇未息，權邛州駐泊巡檢。

translations.literal: Because remaining bandits had not ceased he was made acting inspector stationed at Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With banditry still active he was made acting inspector at Qiong.

sentences.zh: 明年，峽路潰卒鄧紹等復起攻雅州，克明又平之。

translations.literal: The next year routed soldiers of the Gorges route Deng Shao and others again rose and attacked Yazhou; Keming pacified them again.
translations.idiomatic: The next year mutinous Gorges troops under Deng Shao attacked Yazhou again, and Keming suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 還軍邛州，遇賊王珂，戰于延貢鎮，擊以矛，中左踝。

translations.literal: Returning the army to Qiongzhou he met the bandit Wang Ke, fought at Yangong town, and struck with a spear hitting the left ankle.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Qiong he met the bandit Wang Ke at Yangong, struck him with a spear, and wounded his left ankle.

sentences.zh: 後又設伏山下，以數十騎與賊接戰，克明偽北，而所部失期，伏不發。

translations.literal: Later he again set an ambush below the mountain, fought the bandits with several tens of horsemen; Keming feigned retreat but his unit missed the rendezvous and the ambush was not sprung.
translations.idiomatic: He set another ambush below the mountain with a few dozen horsemen; Keming feigned retreat but his men missed the signal and the trap never sprang.

sentences.zh: 克明挺身走，賊追急，乃倚大石引弓三發，斃三人，由是獲免。

translations.literal: Keming straightened his body and fled; the bandits pursued urgently; he then leaned on a great rock and drew the bow three times, killing three men, and thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Keming fled with the enemy in hot pursuit; leaning on a boulder he shot three men dead and escaped.

sentences.zh: 入朝，改內殿崇班，為溫、台等七州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Entering court he was changed to Inner Hall Honored Ban and made overall inspector of Wen, Tai, and seven other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was made Inner Hall Honored Ban and overall inspector of Wen, Tai, and seven other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 景德中，蠻寇邕州，改供備庫副使、知邕州。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era barbarians raided Yongzhou; he was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Supply Depot and made to know Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era barbarians raided Yong; he was made Vice Commissioner of the Supply Depot and prefect of Yong.

sentences.zh: 左、右江蠻洞三十六，克明召其酋長，諭以恩信，是歲承天節，相率來集。

translations.literal: There were thirty-six cave tribes of the left and right River barbarians; Keming summoned their chiefs and instructed them with grace and trust; that year on the Chengtian festival they came in succession to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six tribal chiefs of the left and right rivers were summoned, treated with grace and trust, and came in a body for the Chengtian festival that year.

sentences.zh: 克明慰拊，出衣服遺之，感泣而去。

translations.literal: Keming comforted them, gave out clothing as gifts, and they wept and departed moved.
translations.idiomatic: Keming comforted them, gave them clothing, and they left in tears.

sentences.zh: 獨如洪峒恃險不至，克明諭兩江防遏使黃眾盈引兵攻之，斬其首領陸木前，梟於市。

translations.literal: Only Ru Hong cave relied on its terrain and did not come; Keming instructed the Two-River frontier commissioner Huang Zhongying to lead troops to attack, beheaded their chief Lumuqian, and displayed the head in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ru Hong cave, trusting its terrain, stayed away; Keming had Huang Zhongying attack, beheaded chief Lumuqian, and displayed his head in the market.

sentences.zh: 宜州澄海軍校陳進反。

translations.literal: Chen Jin, a military school officer of the Chenghai Army of Yizhou, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin, an officer of Yizhou's Chenghai Army, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 時鬱江暴漲，州城摧圯，克明率丁夫伐木為連舫，維之水上，狀如郛郭。

translations.literal: At that time the Yujiang rose in violent flood and the prefectural walls collapsed; Keming led laborers to cut timber for linked pontoon boats, moored on the water, shaped like an outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Yujiang flooded and the city walls collapsed; Keming had timber cut for linked boats moored on the water like a wall.

sentences.zh: 又多張旗幟，浮巨筏，陳兵其上，為守禦備。

translations.literal: He also stretched many banners and flags, floated great rafts, arrayed troops on them, and made defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He raised many banners, floated great rafts with troops aboard, and prepared a defense.

sentences.zh: 募溪峒兵三千，而黃眾盈亦濟兵千五百，將趣象州。

translations.literal: He recruited three thousand stream-cave soldiers, and Huang Zhongying also crossed troops numbering one thousand five hundred, about to hurry to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited three thousand tribal troops; Huang Zhongying brought fifteen hundred more to march on Xiang.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫使曹利用約克明會兵，行次貴州，遇賊，大敗之，斬首四百餘級。

translations.literal: When pacification commissioner Cao Liyong arranged to join forces with Keming, marching to Guizhou they met the bandits and inflicted a great defeat, beheading more than four hundred ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Cao Liyong joined Keming; at Guizhou they met the rebels, defeated them, and took more than four hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 賊平，利用專其功。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified Liyong monopolized the merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended Liyong claimed all the credit.

sentences.zh: 代還，真宗問南方事，對稱旨，賜一子官，遷供備庫使，江、淮、兩浙都大提舉捉賊。

translations.literal: On returning to replace his post, Zhenzong inquired about southern affairs; his answers were to the emperor's liking; he granted one son an office, transferred him to Supply Depot commissioner, and made him overall commissioner for capturing bandits in Jiang, Huai, and the two Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhenzong questioned him on the south; pleased with his answers, he gave a son an office, made him Supply Depot commissioner, and overall bandit-catcher for Jiang, Huai, and the two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 克明使人捕賊，輒出私錢資之，以故人人盡力。

translations.literal: Keming whenever he sent men to capture bandits always paid from private funds to support them, and for this reason every man exerted his utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: Keming paid capture parties from his own purse, and his men gave their all.

sentences.zh: 視賊中趫勇者，釋縛，使還捕其黨，前後獲千餘人。

translations.literal: Seeing the boldest among the bandits he released their bonds and had them return to capture their fellows; before and after he obtained more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He freed the boldest captives and sent them back to catch their fellows, taking more than a thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 知江甯府張詠以其事聞，賜錢四十萬，領平州刺史、知辰州。

translations.literal: Jiangning prefect Zhang Yong reported his deeds; he was granted four hundred thousand in cash, held Ping prefecture, and knew Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong of Jiangning reported his work; he received four hundred thousand cash, Ping prefecture, and Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 撫水蠻叛，徙宜、融、桂、昭、柳、象、邕、欽、廉、白十州都巡檢使兼安撫使。

translations.literal: When the Fushui barbarians rebelled he was transferred to overall inspector and pacification commissioner of Yi, Rong, Gui, Zhao, Liu, Xiang, Yong, Qin, Lian, and Bai—ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fushui tribes rebelled he was made overall inspector and pacification commissioner of ten southern prefectures.

sentences.zh: 既至，蠻酋獻藥一器，曰「溪峒藥」，藥箭中人，以是解之可不死。

translations.literal: When he arrived a barbarian chief presented a vessel of medicine, called "stream-cave medicine"; if struck by their poisoned arrows, using this to treat it one would not die.
translations.idiomatic: A tribal chief offered "stream-cave medicine," claiming it cured wounds from poisoned arrows.

sentences.zh: 克明曰：「何以驗之？」

translations.literal: Keming said: "How is it to be verified?"
translations.idiomatic: Keming asked, "How can that be proved?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「請試以雞犬。」

translations.literal: He said: "Please test it on chickens and dogs."
translations.idiomatic: The chief said, "Test it on chickens and dogs."

sentences.zh: 克明曰：「當試以人。」

translations.literal: Keming said: "It should be tested on a man."
translations.idiomatic: Keming said, "Test it on a man."

sentences.zh: 乃取藥箭刺酋股而飲以藥，即死，群蠻慚懼而去。

translations.literal: He thereupon took a poisoned arrow and stabbed the chief's thigh, then had him drink the medicine, and he immediately died; the barbarian masses were ashamed and fearful and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He shot the chief in the thigh with a poisoned arrow, gave him the antidote, and when the chief died the tribes fled in shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，安撫都監王文慶、馬玉出天河砦東，克明與中人楊守珍出環州樟嶺西，磴道危絕，林木深阻，蠻多伏弩以待。

translations.literal: That winter pacification supervisor Wang Wenqing and Ma Yu went out east of Tianhe stockade; Keming with palace attendant Yang Shouzhen went out west of Huanzhou Zhang Ridge; the cliff paths were perilous and forests deep and obstructed; many barbarians set crossbows in ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wenqing and Ma Yu marched east of Tianhe stockade while Keming and Yang Shouzhen went west of Huan's Zhang Ridge over deadly paths where tribes waited in ambush.

sentences.zh: 玉所向力戰，屢敗蠻軍。

translations.literal: Where Yu marched he fought with all his strength and repeatedly defeated barbarian armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yu fought fiercely wherever he marched and repeatedly defeated the tribes.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷意在招附，數詔諭克明，而克明亦憚深入，屢移文止玉。

translations.literal: At that time the court's intent lay in summoning submission; several times edicts instructed Keming, and Keming also feared to go deep, repeatedly sending documents to stop Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought submission and repeatedly instructed Keming, who also feared to advance deep and repeatedly ordered Yu to halt.

sentences.zh: 玉至如門團，為蠻所扼，不得進。

translations.literal: Yu reached Rumenguan and was choked by the barbarians and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reached Rumenguan but was blocked by the tribes and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 克明遷延顧望，月餘，乃至撫水州，與知州蒙承貴等約盟而還。

translations.literal: Keming delayed and looked about; after more than a month he at last reached Fushui prefecture, made covenant with prefect Meng Chenggui and others, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Keming hesitated for more than a month, then reached Fushui, made peace with Meng Chenggui, and returned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知桂州兼管勾溪峒公事，始置溪峒司。

translations.literal: Before long he was made to know Guizhou and concurrently oversee stream-cave affairs, first establishing the Stream-Cave Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Gui, oversaw stream-cave affairs, and established the Stream-Cave Office.

sentences.zh: 又奏閱廣南兩路土軍為忠敢軍。

translations.literal: He also memorialized reviewing the native troops of the two Guangnan routes as the Loyal Bold Army.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reorganize the native troops of the two Guangnan routes as the Loyal Bold Army.

sentences.zh: 州人覆茅為屋，歲多火，克明選北軍教以陶瓦，又激江水入城，以防火災。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture thatched roofs with grass and each year had many fires; Keming selected northern troops to teach tile-making, and also channeled river water into the city to guard against fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Thatched roofs caused yearly fires; Keming taught tile-making and channeled river water into the city against fire.

sentences.zh: 代還，知滁州，徙鼎州。

translations.literal: On returning to replace his post he knew Chuzhou and was transferred to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On return he governed Chu, then was transferred to Ding.

sentences.zh: 會交阯李公蘊寇邕州，以文思使復知邕州。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi's Li Gongyun raided Yongzhou he was again made to know Yongzhou with the title of Literary Thought Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gongyun of Jiaozhi raided Yong, he was again sent as prefect with the title Literary Thought Envoy.

sentences.zh: 既至，遣人入交阯諭以利害，公蘊拜表謝罪。

translations.literal: When he arrived he sent men into Jiaozhi to instruct on advantage and harm; Gongyun submitted a memorial begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he sent envoys to Jiaozhi; Gongyun submitted a memorial begging pardon.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門使，歷知登、舒、邵三州，復徙鼎州，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Upper Pavilion Gate envoy, successively knew Deng, Shu, and Shao prefectures, again moved to Dingzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became Western Upper Pavilion Gate envoy, governed Deng, Shu, and Shao, returned to Ding, and died.

sentences.zh: 張暉，幽州大城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui was a native of Dacheng in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui came from Dacheng in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰初，隸控鶴軍，累遷奉國、弩手都頭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai in Later Tang he was attached to the Crane Control Guard and was repeatedly promoted to head of the Loyal Nation and Crossbow guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Tang Qingtai he joined the Crane Control Guard and rose to head the Loyal Nation and Crossbow guards.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，與武行德奪契丹甲船于河陰。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin Kaiyun he with Wu Xingde seized Khitan armor ships at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin Kaiyun he and Wu Xingde seized Khitan armored ships at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 行德領河陽，以暉為弩手指揮使，復令引兵趣懷州。

translations.literal: Xingde held Heyang and made Hui crossbow guard commander, again ordering him to lead troops to hurry to Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde held Heyang, made Hui crossbow commander, and sent him toward Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹將遁去，因領州軍。

translations.literal: When the Khitan generals were about to flee he thereupon led the prefectural army.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan prepared to withdraw he took command of the prefectural army.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，暉迎于滎陽，授懷州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Han founder entered Bian, Hui welcomed him at Xingyang and was appointed Huaizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder entered Bian, Hui welcomed him at Xingyang and was made prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，郢州刺史慕容業治多不法，以暉為緣漢都巡檢使，領唐州，屯兵至郢州，即代業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, Yingzhou prefect Murong Ye's governance was largely unlawful; Hui was made inspector of the Han frontier route, held Tangzhou, and with troops halted at Yingzhou, at once replacing Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou Ying prefect Murong Ye ruled unlawfully; Hui was sent as frontier inspector with Tangzhou troops, replaced Ye at Ying at once.

sentences.zh: 還京，改郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was changed to Yingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was made prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，劉崇寇晉、絳，召暉為步軍左廂排陣使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun Liu Chong raided Jin and Jiang; Hui was summoned as left-wing infantry battle-array commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Later Zhou Guangshun Liu Chong raided Jin and Jiang; Hui was summoned as left-wing infantry battle-array commander.

sentences.zh: 師還，改沂州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was changed to Yizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 三年，吏民詣闕舉留，俄改冀州。

translations.literal: In the third year officials and people went to court requesting he remain; soon he was changed to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the people petitioned for him to stay; soon he was transferred to Ji.

sentences.zh: 會詔築李晏口、束鹿、安平、博野、百八橋、武強等城，命暉護其役，踰月而就。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered building the cities of Liyankou, Shulu, Anping, Boye, Baibaqiao, Wuqiang, and others, Hui was ordered to oversee the labor and in a little more than a month they were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to build cities at Liyankou, Shulu, Anping, and others, Hui finished the works in little more than a month.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征淮甸，充壕砦都指揮使。

translations.literal: Following the Shizong in campaigning against the Huai region he was made overall trench-and-stockade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Shizong against the Huai and was made overall trench-and-stockade commander.

sentences.zh: 既拔楚、泗，即授泗州。

translations.literal: After Chu and Si were taken he was at once given Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chu and Si fell he was given Sizhou at once.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改耀州，俄為西南面橋道使。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Yaozhou and soon was made southwest bridge-route envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Yao, then made southwest bridge-route envoy.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從征澤、潞，為行營壕砦使，先登陷陣。

translations.literal: In the early Song he followed the campaign against Ze and Lu as field headquarters trench-and-stockade commander, ascending first and breaking the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he campaigned against Ze and Lu as trench commander, leading the assault.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷華州團練使，在郡頗有治狀。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was transferred to regimental trainer of Huazhou and in the prefecture had quite a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made regimental trainer of Hua and governed well.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，太原未下，詔入覲問計，暉對曰：「澤、潞經李筠之叛，瘡痍未復，軍旅一興，恐人力重困。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong Taiyuan had not yet fallen; an edict summoned him to audience to ask his plan; Hui replied: "Ze and Lu after Li Jinyun's rebellion were wounds not yet healed; if the army is raised once, I fear human strength will again be heavily strained.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong's second year, with Taiyuan still holding out, Hui was summoned and said, "Ze and Lu, ravaged by Li Jinyun's rebellion, cannot bear another campaign.

sentences.zh: 不若戢兵育民，俟富庶而後為謀。」

translations.literal: It would be better to sheath arms and nurture the people, wait until they are rich and then make plans."
translations.idiomatic: Sheathe the armies, restore the people, and wait until they are prosperous before striking again."

sentences.zh: 乃賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬，令還州。

translations.literal: He was thereupon granted court robes, gold belt, saddle, and horse and ordered to return to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted robes, a gold belt, saddle, and horse and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方議伐蜀，遷鳳州團練使兼緣邊巡檢壕砦橋道使。

translations.literal: The court was then discussing attacking Shu; he was transferred to regimental trainer of Fengzhou and concurrently frontier inspector of trenches, stockades, and bridge routes.
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated attacking Shu he was made regimental trainer of Feng and frontier inspector of trenches and routes.

sentences.zh: 暉盡得山川險易，因密疏陳之，太祖覽之大悅。

translations.literal: Hui completely obtained the mountains' and rivers' peril and ease and thereby submitted a secret memorial setting them forth; the Taizu on reading it was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hui mapped every pass and defile and sent a secret memorial that delighted Taizu.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，大軍西下，乃以暉充西川行營先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande the great army marched west; he was then made overall vanguard commander of the Western Shu field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande's second year he was made supreme vanguard of the Western Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 督兵開大散關路，躬撫士卒，且役且戰，人忘其勞。

translations.literal: Supervising troops he opened the Dasanguan route, personally comforted the soldiers, working and fighting together, and men forgot their labor.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Dasanguan road, fought alongside his men, and they forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 十二月，至青泥嶺，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he reached Qingni Ridge and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he reached Qingni Ridge and died.

sentences.zh: 天禧五年，暉妻年百五歲，家貧，詣闕自陳。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxi Hui's wife was one hundred five years old, the family was poor, and she went to court to report herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianxi Hui's wife, aged one hundred five, came to court in poverty to plead her case.

sentences.zh: 詔賜束帛，錄其孫永德為三班借職。

translations.literal: An edict granted bolts of silk and enrolled her grandson Yongde as a third-rank borrowed officer.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted silk and enrolled her grandson Yongde as a third-rank borrowed officer.

sentences.zh: 司超，大名元城人。

translations.literal: Si Chao was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Si Chao came from Yuancheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 初事邢帥安叔千。

translations.literal: At first he served Xing military commissioner An Shuqian.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Xing commander An Shuqian.

sentences.zh: 漢祖在太原，超往依之，隸帳下為小校。

translations.literal: When the Han founder was at Taiyuan, Chao went to rely on him and was attached under his tent as a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder was at Taiyuan, Chao joined him as a junior officer in his guard.

sentences.zh: 漢祖將渡河，遣超先領勁騎，由晉、絳趨河陽。

translations.literal: When the Han founder was about to cross the river he sent Chao first to lead fierce cavalry by Jin and Jiang to hurry to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before crossing the river the Han founder sent Chao ahead with elite cavalry toward Heyang by way of Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，以超為鄆州必敵指揮使。

translations.literal: When he entered Bian, Chao was made Yingzhou Bidi commander.
translations.idiomatic: On entering Bian he was made Bidi commander of Ying.

sentences.zh: 時京東諸州寇盜充斥，以超為宋、宿、亳三州游奕巡檢使。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures east of the capital were full of bandits; Chao was made roaming inspector of Song, Su, and Bo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits filled the eastern prefectures; Chao was made roaming inspector of Song, Su, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 改宿州西固鎮守禦都指揮使，移屯潁州下蔡鎮。

translations.literal: He was changed to overall defense commander of Xigu town in Suzhou and moved his encampment to Xiaxia town in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defender of Suzhou's Xigu and moved his camp to Ying's Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 屢與淮人戰，有功。

translations.literal: He repeatedly fought the Huai men with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Huai repeatedly with success.

sentences.zh: 周世宗命宰相李穀討淮南，以超為步軍先鋒副都指揮使，又為廬、壽、光、黃等州巡檢使。

translations.literal: The Zhou Shizong ordered chief minister Li Gu to campaign against Huainan and made Chao deputy overall vanguard commander of the foot army and inspector of Lu, Shou, Guang, and Huang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong ordered Li Gu against Huainan and made Chao deputy foot vanguard and inspector of Lu, Shou, Guang, and Huang.

sentences.zh: 大敗淮人三千餘眾于盛唐縣，獲棹船四十餘艘，禽其監軍高弼、果毅指揮使許萬以獻。

translations.literal: He inflicted a great defeat on more than three thousand Huai men at Sheng Tang county, obtained more than forty oar-boats, and captured their supervising army Gao Bi and resolute commander Xu Wan and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He routed more than three thousand Huai troops at Sheng Tang, seized forty boats, and captured Gao Bi and Xu Wan.

sentences.zh: 時黃州未下，即命超遙領刺史兼樓櫓戰棹右廂都校。

translations.literal: At that time Huangzhou had not yet fallen; he was at once ordered to hold Huang prefecture concurrently and was also right-wing commander of tower-ships and war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou had not yet fallen; he was made acting prefect of Huang and right-wing commander of the war fleet.

sentences.zh: 師還，改光州刺史，敗吳軍千餘于麻城北。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was changed to Guang prefect and defeated more than a thousand Wu troops north of Ma city.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made prefect of Guang and defeated more than a thousand Wu troops north of Ma.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年冬，與王審琦攻舒州，敗吳軍三千，先禽刺史施仁望獻於行在。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Xiande he with Wang Shenqi attacked Shuzhou, defeated three thousand Wu troops, and first captured prefect Shi Renwang and presented him at the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiande he and Wang Shenqi attacked Shu, routed three thousand Wu troops, and captured Prefect Shi Renwang first.

sentences.zh: 即以超為舒州團練使。

translations.literal: He was at once made regimental trainer of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once made regimental trainer of Shu.

sentences.zh: 【評論】

translations.literal: Commentary
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 論曰：昔許子卒于師，葬之加等。

translations.literal: The comment says: In old times when Xu died in the army he was buried with raised rites.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When Xu died on campaign the Spring and Autumn raised his burial rites.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》書之，所以褒臣節而儆官守也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn records it in order to praise ministerial integrity and warn officials in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn records this to honor loyal service and warn those who hold office.

sentences.zh: 業、罕儒、光實咸當捍城之寄，臨戎力戰，歿於敵境。

translations.literal: Ye, Hanru, and Guangshi all bore the charge of defending the cities; facing the enemy they fought with all their strength and died in enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye, Jing Hanru, and Cao Guangshi all held the frontier defense; each fought to the last and fell in enemy country.

sentences.zh: 雖罕儒恃勇不戒，光實甘賊遷之言，失在輕敵，然其忘軀徇節，誠可嘉也。

translations.literal: Although Hanru relied on courage and did not take warning, and Guangshi was pleased with Jiqian's words of relocation, their fault lay in despising the enemy—yet in forgetting their bodies and following integrity they are truly worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru was reckless and Guangshi trusted Jiqian's false surrender—both erred through contempt for the enemy—yet in giving their lives for duty they remain deeply admirable.

sentences.zh: 業本太原驍將，感太宗寵遇，思有以報。

translations.literal: Ye was originally a fierce general of Taiyuan; moved by Taizong's gracious treatment he thought to find some means of repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ye was a famed warrior of Taiyuan who, grateful for Taizong's favor, longed to repay it in service.

sentences.zh: 常勝之家，千慮一失。

translations.literal: A house that is ever victorious—in a thousand plans there is one lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Even invincible commanders err once in a thousand calculations.

sentences.zh: 然其素得士心。

translations.literal: Yet he had long won the hearts of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had always won his soldiers' hearts.

sentences.zh: 部卒不忍離去，從之以歿，則忠義之風概可見矣。

translations.literal: His subordinates could not bear to leave him and followed him to death—then the spirit of loyalty and righteousness may be seen.
translations.idiomatic: His men refused to abandon him and died at his side—proof enough of his loyal spirit.

sentences.zh: 嗣與延昭並克紹勳伐。

translations.literal: Si and Yanzhao both were able to continue their fathers' military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Si and Yang Yanzhao both carried on their fathers' martial legacy.

sentences.zh: 延昭久居邊閫，總戎訓士，威名方略，聞于敵人，於嗣為優。

translations.literal: Yanzhao long dwelt on the frontier command, oversaw troops and trained soldiers; his martial renown and stratagems were heard among the enemy—compared with Si he was superior.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao spent decades on the frontier, training troops whose fame reached the enemy; in reputation and strategy he surpassed Si.

sentences.zh: 暉于危時則有陷陣之功，平日則獻息戎之諫。

translations.literal: Hui in times of peril had the merit of breaking enemy lines; in ordinary times he presented counsel to rest the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui led the assault in crisis and counseled peace in calmer days.

sentences.zh: 超頻戰以清淮海，其忠誠勇果，率有可尚者焉。

translations.literal: Chao fought repeatedly to pacify the Huai and sea regions; his loyalty, courage, and resolution were on the whole worthy of esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Si Chao fought again and again to clear the Huai and the coast; his loyalty and courage were admirable throughout.
